confirmedRules.name: Flight is auto-approved on a validated save
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When a flight log is saved with full validation and it is not yet approved, the system marks it approved, records the saving user as approver and stamps the approval time in UTC.
confirmedRules.given: A flight log with IsApproved = False, saved by user 'jdoe' who holds Fleet edit rights, and the flight passes Validate(EnforceValidation=True)
confirmedRules.when: FlightManager.Insert or Update runs with EnforceValidation = True (the default overloads)
confirmedRules.then: IsApproved = True, ApprovedBy = 'jdoe', UtcDateApproved = current UTC time; the record is persisted with StampUserName = 'jdoe'. If EnforceValidation = False the flight is saved without being approved.
confirmedRules.parameters: EnforceValidation flag (default True via Save/Insert/Update 2-arg overloads); same logic duplicated in Update at FlightManager.vb:60-66
edgeCases: Already-approved flights keep their original approver and approval date on later edits; approval is never revoked by edits
EnforceValidation=False is the only way to save a draft/unapproved flight
Approval is set before FlightDB write; a DB failure leaves the in-memory object marked approved
Update path does not adjust engine-run times (only Insert calls DateTimeAdjustFlightEngineRunList)
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Update (lines 50-84) does not call DateTimeAdjustFlightEngineRunList, so engine-run local/UTC times are not recomputed when a flight's date, departure time or location is edited; Insert does (line 116).

confirmedRules.name: Flight starting airframe hours = Hobbs start + meter offset
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A flight's starting airframe hours are computed as the Hobbs meter start reading plus the meter offset in use, rounded to one decimal place.
confirmedRules.given: A flight with HobbsStart = 1234.56 and UsedMeterOffset = 10.0
confirmedRules.when: The flight is inserted or updated
confirmedRules.then: AirframeHoursStart = '1,244.6' (HobbsStart + UsedMeterOffset, formatted '#,##0.0' i.e. rounded to 1 decimal with thousands separator)
confirmedRules.parameters: Format mask '#,##0.0' (1 decimal); same formula at FlightManager.vb:104
edgeCases: Value is stored as a formatted string with thousands separator, so later CDec parsing depends on culture
Non-numeric HobbsStart/UsedMeterOffset raises a conversion error
Rounding uses .NET Format (away-from-zero midpoint)
confirmedRules.smeQuestion:
P0 panel doubts spec fidelity: P0 is justified. Airframe hours are the main figure a flight log tracker produces. They feed aircraft time and maintenance tracking, which is a safety and data-integrity concern. Every flight Insert and Update sets the value (FlightManager.vb:58 and :104).

The card is not faithful on rounding. It says the sum is "HobbsStart + UsedMeterOffset, rounded to 1 decimal". The code rounds each input first and then adds them:
- Flight.HobbsStart (Flight.vb:649-651) and Flight.UsedMeterOffset (Flight.vb:571-573) are String properties. Their getters return Format(_decimal, _meterMask), and _meterMask is "#,##0.0;-#,##0.0" (Flight.vb:17). So CDec(Flight.HobbsStart) is already rounded to 1 decimal before the addition.
- The sum is then formatted with "#,##0.0" and assigned to the AirframeHoursStart String setter (Flight.vb:664-676). The setter parses it back with CDec and stores a Decimal. The getter re-formats that Decimal with _meterMask.

The card's example (1234.56 + 10.0 gives 1,244.6) happens to come out the same either way. A counter-example shows the difference: HobbsStart 1234.45 with offset 0.05. The code computes 1234.5 + 0.1 (.NET custom formats round midpoints away from zero) = 1234.6. The card's formula gives round(1234.50) = 1234.5. The setters accept values with more than 1 decimal (CDec(value), e.g. Flight.vb:657), so this case can happen.

Other details the card leaves out:
- A null or non-numeric input becomes 0.
- The stored value is a Decimal parsed from the formatted string, not the string '1,244.6'. The thousands-separator round trip depends on the server culture.
- On Update, DateTimeAdjustFlightObject runs before the calculation. That ordering does not affect the sum.

Fix the Then clause: AirframeHoursStart = round1(round1(HobbsStart) + round1(UsedMeterOffset)), with midpoints rounded away from zero. Add the 1234.45 + 0.05 = 1234.6 edge case. No injection-style text was found in the cited lines.

confirmedRules.name: Flight departure/return times converted to UTC with overnight rollover
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Departure and return local date-times are built from the flight date plus the entered times; if the return hour is earlier than the departure hour the return is moved to the next day, and both are converted to UTC using the location's time zone.
confirmedRules.given: Flight date 2026-07-01 at a location with offset -5, departure 22:00, return 01:30
confirmedRules.then: Departure local = 2026-07-01 22:00; Return local = 2026-07-02 01:30; UTC values are the local values minus the effective offset (see DST rule), with the return UTC also shifted +1 day
confirmedRules.parameters: Rollover test compares the hour component only
edgeCases: Departure 10:45, return 10:15 (same hour, earlier minutes) is NOT rolled to next day, giving a negative-duration flight
Flights longer than 24h cannot be represented
Invalid time text yields DateTime.MinValue silently (see time format rule)
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Hour-only comparison misses same-hour overnight returns (e.g. depart 23:50, return 23:10 next day).

confirmedRules.name: Local-to-UTC conversion with location daylight-saving window
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A local time is converted to UTC by subtracting the location's time-zone offset, plus the daylight-saving offset when the location observes DST and the local time falls within its configured DST start/end dates (inclusive).
confirmedRules.given: Location TimeZoneOffset = -5, DaylightSavingTime = True, DaylightSavingOffset = 1, DST window 2026-03-08 to 2026-11-01; local time 2026-07-01 08:30
confirmedRules.when: Any flight, comment or engine-run time is converted
confirmedRules.then: Effective offset = -4; UTC = 08:30 - (-4h) = 12:30 on 2026-07-01
confirmedRules.parameters: Per-location TimeZoneOffset, DaylightSavingOffset, DaylightSavingBegin, DaylightSavingEnd (inclusive bounds)
edgeCases: DST window is compared as full date-times; if DaylightSavingEnd is a date at 00:00, times later on the end date are treated as non-DST
DST window values are stored per location and must be maintained yearly
Fractional offsets (e.g. 5.5) supported via Double

confirmedRules.name: Late-departure comments and engine runs roll to next day
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Comment and engine-run times are placed on the departure date, but when the flight departs at 16:00 or later and the entry's hour is more than one hour before the departure hour, the entry is moved to the next day.
confirmedRules.given: Departure local 2026-07-01 20:00; a pilot comment at 02:15 and an engine run 01:00-01:20
confirmedRules.then: Comment local = 2026-07-02 02:15; engine run 2026-07-02 01:00-01:20; UTC values shifted +1 day as well
confirmedRules.parameters: Late-departure threshold 16 (hour); tolerance 1 hour before departure
edgeCases: Comment with blank time defaults to the departure time
Departure at 15:00 with comment at 01:00 next morning is NOT rolled (stays on departure date)
Departure 20:00, comment 19:30 (within 1h before) stays same day
Engine run end is rolled only together with the start; an end time past midnight with start before midnight is not rolled
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is 16:00 the intended cut-off for 'night flight' rollover, and should early-departure flights whose events cross midnight also roll over?

confirmedRules.name: Time-of-day entry format
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Flight, comment and engine-run times are only accepted as 12-hour h:mm AM/PM or 24-hour H:mm (colon or period separator); otherwise no date-time is produced.
confirmedRules.given: Flight date 2026-07-01 and time text '7.45 pm' or '19:45'
confirmedRules.then: Result is 2026-07-01 19:45; for '25:00' or '7pm' the result is an empty DateTime (0001-01-01) with no error raised
edgeCases: Single minute digit after a 12h hour is accepted ('7:4 PM')
A period separator passes the regex but CDate of '19.45' may fail depending on culture
Failure is silent: default DateTime flows into UTC math and persistence
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Invalid time text produces DateTime.MinValue silently rather than a validation error.

confirmedRules.name: Aircraft configuration meter chaining
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: For a new aircraft the first configuration sets the aircraft's starting and current airframe hours and offset; for an existing aircraft a new configuration starts at the aircraft's current airframe hours, closes the previous latest configuration at that reading, and becomes the source of the aircraft's meter offset and unit.
confirmedRules.given: Existing aircraft (Id 42) with AirframeHoursCurrent = 512.3 and latest configuration started at 300.0; new configuration offset 2.5, unit 'hours'
confirmedRules.then: New config MeterStart = 512.3; previous config MeterEnd = 512.3; aircraft AirframeHoursOffset = 2.5 and MeterUnitId = new unit. For a brand-new aircraft (Id 0) with config MeterStart 0 and offset 2.5: AirframeHoursStart = 0, AirframeHoursCurrent = 0, Offset = 2.5
confirmedRules.parameters: New in-memory children receive negative temporary ids (NewAircraftConfigurationId decremented)
edgeCases: Aircraft fields are changed before the configuration is validated; a failed validation leaves the aircraft's offset/unit already modified
Latest configuration is the one with the highest MeterStart (see separate rule)
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Aircraft offset/unit/hours are mutated before AircraftConfiguration.Validate(); an invalid configuration still alters the aircraft in memory.

confirmedRules.name: Saved aircraft configurations are immutable
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Once an aircraft configuration has been saved it can be neither edited nor removed; only unsaved (pending) configurations may be changed or removed, and removing one reopens the prior latest configuration.
confirmedRules.given: Aircraft with saved configuration Id 17 and an unsaved pending configuration Id -1
confirmedRules.when: User attempts to update or remove configuration 17, or removes configuration -1
confirmedRules.then: Update/remove of 17 throws 'editing/deleting an existing Aircraft Configuration is not allowed'; removing -1 sets the remaining latest configuration's MeterEnd = 0 and restores the aircraft offset from it
confirmedRules.parameters: Persisted = Id > 0
edgeCases: Updating a pending configuration resets its MeterStart to the aircraft's current hours and re-applies offset and unit
If no configuration remains, the code intends to zero AirframeHoursStart/Current/Offset
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: RetrieveLatestAircraftConfiguration always returns a New object (never Nothing), so the 'no configurations left' branch that zeroes airframe hours (lines 155-158) is unreachable; instead MeterEnd/offset are set on an empty placeholder object and the aircraft offset becomes 0 implicitly.

confirmedRules.name: Latest configuration and latest location selection
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The aircraft's latest configuration is the one with the highest meter start reading; the latest location is intended to be the one with the most recent arrival date.
confirmedRules.given: Configurations with MeterStart 0, 300.0, 512.3
confirmedRules.then: The configuration starting at 512.3 is returned; if all start at 0, an empty configuration is returned
confirmedRules.parameters: Comparison is strictly greater-than against an initial 0 value
edgeCases: A sole configuration starting at meter 0 is never selected as latest
Ties keep the first found
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: RetrieveLatestAircraftLocation initialises the candidate to Nothing and then reads aircraftLocation.ArrivalDate, which throws a NullReferenceException for any aircraft that has locations.

confirmedRules.name: Single current location per aircraft
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Only one aircraft location assignment may be flagged as the last (current) test location; flagging a new one clears the flag on all others and sets the aircraft's current location, and removing the flagged one clears the aircraft's current location.
confirmedRules.given: Aircraft at location A (LastLocation = True) and a new assignment to location B with LastLocation = True
confirmedRules.when: The new location is inserted or updated
confirmedRules.then: A.LastLocation = False, B.LastLocation = True, Aircraft.CurrentLocationId = B
confirmedRules.parameters: Persisted locations (Id > 0) removed are queued on AircraftLocationDeleteList
edgeCases: Removing the current location sets CurrentLocationId = 0
Unsaved (negative id) locations are discarded without a delete record
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should an aircraft be allowed to be assigned to the same location more than once? UpdateAircraftLocation matches the existing row by LocationId rather than AircraftLocationId.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: UpdateAircraftLocation (line 265) matches by LocationId, so if the aircraft has two assignments to the same location the wrong record may be replaced.

confirmedRules.name: Comment type validation and aircraft comment ordering
confirmedRules.source: FLTBizObjects/BusinessLogic/AircraftManager.vb:285-329 (InsertGenericComment / RemoveGenericComment) together with FLTBizObjects/BusinessLogic/AircraftManager.vb:496-545 (ValidateGenericComment / SortGenericCommentList); temp-id seed at FLTBizObjects/BusinessObject/Aircraft.vb:66
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A generic comment is validated according to its source type (aircraft, flight, work-order engineer or mechanic comment); unknown types are rejected; aircraft comments are kept sorted newest first and only aircraft comments can be removed from an aircraft.
confirmedRules.given: A generic comment with SourceTable 'AircraftComment' dated 2026-07-02 added to an aircraft whose existing comment is dated 2026-07-01
confirmedRules.then: Comment validated as AircraftComment, gets a negative temp id, and is placed before the 2026-07-01 comment
confirmedRules.parameters: Accepted types: aircraftcomment, flightcomment, woengineercomment, womechaniccomment (case-insensitive)
edgeCases: Unknown SourceTable -> broken rule 'Unable to determine the Comment Type'
Any warning (not just error) blocks the save because WarningsList count must be 0
Removing a non-AircraftComment throws 'Removing a comment that is not an Aircraft Comment is not allowed' (lines 307-329)
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Citation was corrected by referee (The behavior is real, but the cited range only covers part of it. Lines 496-545 contain ValidateGenericComment and SortGenericCommentList. ValidateGenericComment branches on LCase(SourceTable) into aircraftcomment, flightcomment, woengineercomment and womechaniccomment, and adds a "Unable to determine the Comment Type" BrokenRule for any other value. SortGenericCommentList is an insertion sort that puts the newest CommentDate first. The rest of the rule is outside that range. The spec's When/Then step lives in InsertGenericComment at lines 285-305: it forces SourceTable to "AircraftComment" (line 286), validates, assigns SourceID from Aircraft.NewGenericCommentId and then decrements it (lines 289-290; the counter starts at -1 per FLTBizObjects/BusinessObject/Aircraft.vb:66, so the temp ids are negative), adds the comment and sorts it. The "only aircraft comments can be removed" restriction is in RemoveGenericComment at lines 307-329. Its comparison is case-sensitive (SourceTable = "AircraftComment"), unlike the case-insensitive check during validation. If validation fails on insert, the comment's broken rules are copied to the aircraft and an exception is thrown. Everything here is executable code, and I found no instruction-shaped text.) — confirm FLTBizObjects/BusinessLogic/AircraftManager.vb:285-329 (InsertGenericComment / RemoveGenericComment) together with FLTBizObjects/BusinessLogic/AircraftManager.vb:496-545 (ValidateGenericComment / SortGenericCommentList); temp-id seed at FLTBizObjects/BusinessObject/Aircraft.vb:66 is the authoritative implementation.

confirmedRules.name: Module-based authorization for every business operation
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Each operation checks the user's view or edit permission on a named module; super-users can do everything, the current program manager can do everything except Security and AppConfig, and other users need an explicit role-module permission.
confirmedRules.given: User 'pilot1' whose role grants Fleet CanView but not CanEdit
confirmedRules.when: The user opens a flight and then tries to save it
confirmedRules.then: GetItem succeeds; Save throws 'Can't update - user is not authorized'
confirmedRules.parameters: Module mapping: Fleet (Aircraft, AircraftInfo, Flight, FlightInfo, FlightKeyInfo, Location, Region, Route); Documents (DocumentInfo, DocumentManager, DocumentType view); System (DocumentType edit); Security (FltModule, FltRole, FltRoleModulePermissions, FltUserInRole); Program (Program get/edit/clone); Export (FltExportManager). Rule engine resolved in fltIdentityManager.vb:97-123
edgeCases: Edit permission does not imply view permission in the permission check
DocumentTypeManager edits require the 'System' module (DocumentType.vb:106-108) while viewing requires 'Documents'
Program managers cannot manage Security even within their own program
Null identity throws

confirmedRules.name: Operations that bypass authorization
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Several operations perform no permission check: all spreadsheet reports always allow viewing, document file content can be read or overwritten, aircraft-test links can be added/removed, program lists can be read, and user accounts can be listed, created, updated, deleted or unlocked by any caller.
confirmedRules.given: A user with no roles at all
confirmedRules.when: They request the Fleet spreadsheet, download document 5's stream, or call FltUserManager.Delete
confirmedRules.then: The operation succeeds (CanView returns True unconditionally; other methods never call CanView/CanEdit)
confirmedRules.parameters: Affected: RptFleetManager/RptLocationsManager/RptRegionsManager/RptConfigValuesManager.CanView (always True); DocumentManager.GetStream/PutStream (DocumentManager.vb:13-27); AircraftTestXrefManager Insert/Delete/lists (AircraftTestXrefManager.vb:14-65); ProgramManager.GetList (ProgramManager.vb:14-26); FltUserManager all methods (FltUserManager.vb:16-91)
edgeCases: DocumentManager defines CanView/CanEdit but never calls them
Callers in the UI layer may enforce checks not visible here
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Are reports, document streams, test assignments and user administration meant to be open to every authenticated user, or is authorization enforced in the web layer?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Missing authorization on user administration (create/delete/unlock users) and document overwrite is a likely security gap.

confirmedRules.name: Overridable warnings versus hard errors
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Broken rules that are overridable become warnings the user can acknowledge; a warning only stops blocking once the user has explicitly overridden the same warning previously shown; non-overridable rules are always blocking errors.
confirmedRules.given: A flight with an overridable warning 'Hobbs jump > threshold' that was shown on the previous submit and the user ticked override
confirmedRules.then: The warning is marked OverRideRule = True, listed in WarningsList, and does not count as an error; a first-time warning or non-overridden one counts as 1 error
confirmedRules.parameters: Match on previous warning by PropertyName + RuleIdentifier + Message (existence), then by RuleIdentifier (override lookup)
edgeCases: If the message text changes between submits the warning is treated as new and blocks again
Multiple previous warnings with the same RuleIdentifier add the rule to WarningsList multiple times and may count multiple errors

confirmedRules.name: Flight key selection must be complete and consistent
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Before a flight log is opened, the user must pick a location, aircraft, valid flight date and work shift, and the aircraft must exist, the location must exist, the aircraft must be assigned to that location, and the work shift must exist.
confirmedRules.given: Aircraft 42, location 7, date '2026-07-01', work shift 2, where aircraft 42 is not assigned to location 7
confirmedRules.then: ErrorsList contains 'Aircraft is not assigned to selected Location'
confirmedRules.parameters: Zero id means 'not chosen'; date normalised to yyyy-MM-dd
edgeCases: Any missing field short-circuits the database checks
Blank date -> 'Please provide a flight date.'; non-date -> 'Please provide a valid flight date.'

confirmedRules.name: User password lifecycle
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: New users receive a system-generated password (salted hash stored) emailed to them; changing a password requires the correct old password and matching confirmation; an admin can regenerate and email a new password; unlocking an account clears the lockout and resets failed attempts to zero.
confirmedRules.given: User 'jdoe' with stored salted hash
confirmedRules.when: jdoe changes password with a wrong old password
confirmedRules.then: 'Old Password not valid!' is raised; with correct old password but mismatched confirmation, 'Confirm New Password does not match New Password value!'; otherwise a new salt+hash is stored
confirmedRules.parameters: Generator/hash from fltPassword; email settings WebmasterEmailAddress, SMTPServer, SysName, LoginURL, appPrefix from app config
edgeCases: Updates performed with an empty identity are stamped 'Password Change'
Email send failures are logged and swallowed, so a new user may never learn the password
No password-strength check on user-chosen passwords in this layer
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Plain-text generated passwords are sent by email, and email failure is silently ignored after the account is created.

confirmedRules.name: Program cloning copies setup data
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Creating a program from a source program copies its active roles (with module permissions and user memberships), regions, locations with their routes, weight definitions and all lookup values into the new program.
confirmedRules.given: Source program 3 with 2 roles, 5 locations each with routes, and lookup lists
confirmedRules.when: Clone(3, newProgram) is run by a user with Program edit rights
confirmedRules.then: A new program is inserted and every active, non-deleted child is re-created under the new program id, with users added to the corresponding new roles
confirmedRules.parameters: Filters: IsActive=1, IsDeleted=0 for roles/locations/routes/weights; lookups active only
edgeCases: Not transactional: a mid-way failure leaves a partially cloned program
Regions are copied without updating StampUserName
Aircraft, flights and documents are not copied

confirmedRules.name: Default list filters show only active, non-deleted, approved records
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Standard list views return only active, non-deleted records, and the default flight lists additionally return only approved flights.
confirmedRules.given: Aircraft 42 with 10 flights, 2 unapproved and 1 deleted
confirmedRules.when: The default FlightInfoManager.GetList(aircraft, text, location) is used
confirmedRules.then: 7 flights are returned (IsApproved=1, IsActive=1, IsDeleted=0)
confirmedRules.parameters: IsApprovedFilter=1, IsActiveFilter=1, IsDeletedFilter=0, RowStart/RowCount=-1 (all); same active/non-deleted defaults in AircraftInfoManager.vb:14-17, ProgramManager, FltUserManager, FltModuleManager, report managers
edgeCases: Draft flights saved with EnforceValidation=False are hidden from default lists
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Confirm that filter value 1 means 'only approved' (rather than 'any') in FlightInfoDB.GetList.

confirmedRules.name: Incremental flight export since a change date
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The download export writes all programs, aircraft, configurations and locations, but includes only flights modified on or after the requested 'changes since' date; with no date, everything since 2000-01-01 is exported, and the file is written to a temp name then renamed.
confirmedRules.given: ChangesSince = 2026-06-01 and a flight last modified 2026-05-31
confirmedRules.then: That flight is omitted; a flight modified 2026-06-01T00:00 or later is included (filter at lines 295-301)
confirmedRules.parameters: Default ChangesSince 01-Jan-2000; file name Download_<appPrefix>_<yyyyMMddTHHmmssz>.xml; requires Export module view right
edgeCases: Programs, aircraft, configs and locations are always exported regardless of the date
Work orders section is always empty (ProcessOneWorkOrder is a stub)
UtcDateModified is compared to ChangesSince without time-zone normalisation

confirmedRules.name: Export auto-creates missing aircraft-location assignments
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: If an aircraft has flights logged at a location it is not formally assigned to, the export creates the aircraft-location assignment (arrival = now, stamped 'export') and includes it.
confirmedRules.given: Aircraft 42 has flights at location 9 but no AircraftLocation row for 9
confirmedRules.then: A new AircraftLocation (AircraftId 42, LocationId 9, ArrivalDate = UtcNow, StampUserName 'export') is inserted in the database and exported
confirmedRules.parameters: StampUserName 'export'
edgeCases: Runs on every export until the assignment exists
Bypasses AircraftLocation validation and LastLocation handling
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: A read-only export operation writes data directly through the DAL, bypassing business validation and authorization for edits.

confirmedRules.name: Export meter and check-value conversions
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: In the export, a liquid fill's meter reading is reported as the Hobbs reading plus the flight's meter offset, oil/hydraulic levels are expressed in quarters, and checklist answers are mapped 1 = Yes, -1 = No, anything else = Not Answered.
confirmedRules.given: Liquid fill Hobbs 101.2, flight UsedMeterOffset 10.0; PreFlightFtiOK = 1, PostFlightFtiOK = 0; oil level 3
confirmedRules.then: LiquidFillMeter = '111.2'; PreFlightFtiOK = 'Yes'; PostFlightFtiOK = 'Not Answered'; OilLevelIndicatorStart = '3/4'
confirmedRules.parameters: Format '#,##9.9'; check codes 1/-1/other (CheckYesNo at lines 506-517)
edgeCases: Liquid fill object is mutated in memory during export
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Line 355 exports PreFlightTelemetryCheckComplete using the PostFlightTelemetryCheckComplete value; String.Format is called with a numeric first argument and '#,##9.9' as an argument, so the composite format is likely not applied as intended.

confirmedRules.name: Export UTC offset notation
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Exported local date-times carry a UTC offset suffix computed from the difference between local and UTC values.
confirmedRules.parameters: Sign '+' only when the hour difference is > 0
edgeCases: Zero offset produces '-00:00'
Positive half-hour offsets under 1 hour (e.g. +00:30) are rendered with '-'
Location TimeZone element is 'UTC' & Format(offset,'00'), so +5 renders 'UTC05' and -5 'UTC-05' (line 269)
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Sign logic uses hours only, mis-signing zero and sub-hour positive offsets.

confirmedRules.name: Spreadsheet reports of active reference data
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Fleet, location, region and configuration-value spreadsheets list only active (and non-deleted where supported) records for the chosen program, and return no workbook when there is nothing to report.
confirmedRules.given: Program 3 with 4 active aircraft and 1 inactive
confirmedRules.then: A workbook with sheet 'Fleet' and 4 data rows (airframe start/current/offset, meter unit, engine hours) is returned; for a program with no active aircraft, Nothing is returned
confirmedRules.parameters: IsActiveFilter=1, IsDeletedFilter=0; same pattern in RptLocationsManager.vb:13-36, RptRegionsManager, RptConfigValuesManager.vb:13-36 (by lookup name)
edgeCases: Locations sheet is named 'Locactions' (typo)
Any data error is reported only as 'An application error occurred'

confirmedRules.name: New versus existing record on save; pending child edits
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A record with no concurrency id (empty or '0') is inserted, otherwise updated; child items added in the editor get negative temporary ids, and removing a previously saved child (positive id) queues it for deletion while removing an unsaved one simply discards it; a failing child passes its broken rules up to the parent.
confirmedRules.given: A flight with saved liquid fill Id 55 and unsaved liquid fill Id -1
confirmedRules.then: Fill 55 is added to LiquidFillDeleteList; fill -1 is dropped; the flight's Save (ConcurrencyId non-empty) performs an Update
confirmedRules.parameters: Same pattern for FlightComment, FlightEngineRun, FlightRegionTime, AircraftLocation, GenericComment and AircraftTest; Save routing at FlightManager.vb:37-43
edgeCases: Removing a test (AircraftManager.vb:374-388) always queues a delete regardless of id
Not-found removals raise 'record not found in collection'

confirmedRules.name: Login account eligibility check
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A user can only attempt to log in if the login name exists, the account is not deleted and the account is active; every one of these failures shows the same generic message.
confirmedRules.given: A login name 'jdoe' whose user record has IsActive = False
confirmedRules.then: Login is refused with 'Failed Login Attempt - either Username or Password is incorrect'. The real reason is only written to the log.
confirmedRules.parameters: Check order: user exists, then not IsDeleted, then IsActive
edgeCases: Unknown, deleted and inactive accounts all get the same message, so the user cannot tell whether an account exists
These checks run before the lockout and password checks, so attempts on inactive or deleted accounts never count toward lockout

confirmedRules.name: Failed-login lockout threshold
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Each wrong password adds one to the user's failure count. When a wrong password arrives and the count already equals the maximum allowed minus one, the account is locked and the lock time is recorded.
confirmedRules.given: MaximumLoginFailuresAllowed = 5 and a user with FailedPasswordAttemptCount = 4
confirmedRules.when: The user enters a wrong password
confirmedRules.then: IsLockedOut = True and UtcFailedPasswordAttemptWindowStart = now (UTC). The user sees 'Login failures exceeded maximum allowed attempts - user account is locked out'. If the count were 0 to 3, it would go up by 1 and the user would see the generic failure message.
confirmedRules.parameters: MaximumLoginFailuresAllowed: AppSettings key, set to 5 in FLTWebApp/Web.config:80 and FLTRestService/Web.config:40; the code falls back to 3 if the key is missing or not numeric (FLTBizObjects/DataAccess/AppConfig.vb:46-57)
edgeCases: The locking attempt does not add to the counter, so with a maximum of 5 the stored count stays at 4 while the account is locked
The 'window start' timestamp is set only at lockout, so it is really the lockout start time, not the start of a rolling window of failed attempts
Failures are never reset by time unless the account is locked; 4 failures spread over months still lock on the 5th

confirmedRules.name: Lockout expiry and failure-counter reset
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A locked account stays locked for the lockout duration after it was locked; after that, the next login attempt unlocks it and clears the failure count. A successful login also clears the lock and the count.
confirmedRules.given: LockoutDuration = 5 minutes and a user locked at 10:00 UTC
confirmedRules.when: The user tries to log in at 10:03 UTC, and again at 10:06 UTC
confirmedRules.then: At 10:03 the login is refused with 'User account is locked out - try again later', and the password is not checked. At 10:06 the account is unlocked and FailedPasswordAttemptCount is set to 0, and then the password is checked as normal.
confirmedRules.parameters: Lockout_Duration: AppSettings key 'LockoutDuration', default 5 minutes (FLTBizObjects/DataAccess/AppConfig.vb:32-43). Elapsed time uses DateDiff in whole minutes (truncated). A successful login also resets the lock and count (fltIdentityManager.vb:68-71).
edgeCases: DateDiff in minutes counts minute-boundary crossings, so the real lockout can be up to about 59 seconds shorter than configured
If the password is wrong right after the auto-unlock, counting restarts from 0
States: Active (count 0..max-1), then LockedOut (with timestamp), then auto-unlocked after the duration on the next attempt

confirmedRules.name: Password hashing with per-user salt
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Passwords are stored as Base64(SHA-512(salt + password)). The salt is 96 random bytes in Base64 (128 characters), and the hash is computed over a fixed 256-byte buffer padded with zeros.
confirmedRules.given: A user salt of 128 Base64 characters and the password 'Pilot2026'
confirmedRules.then: Salt + 'Pilot2026' (137 characters) is copied one byte per character into a 256-byte zero-filled buffer, SHA-512 hashes the whole buffer, and the Base64 result must exactly match the stored password.
confirmedRules.parameters: Salt size: 96 bytes from RNGCryptoServiceProvider. Hash buffer: 256 bytes. Algorithm: SHA-512 with a single iteration.
edgeCases: A password longer than 128 characters (with a 128-character salt) overflows the 256-byte buffer and causes an error
Characters with a code above 255 (non-Latin-1) cannot fit in a byte and cause an overflow error, so such passwords cannot be used
A rewrite must hash the same zero-padded 256-byte buffer, or existing password hashes will stop matching
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: A single unstretched SHA-512 is weak for password storage, and the fixed buffer limits password length and character set.

confirmedRules.name: Random password generation
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: System-generated passwords are 10 characters long. Each character is drawn from digits, upper case letters, lower case letters and 25 punctuation symbols, using a secure random byte taken modulo 87.
confirmedRules.given: A random byte of 200
confirmedRules.then: 200 mod 87 = 26, which falls in 10..35, so the character is 'A' + 16 = 'Q'
confirmedRules.parameters: Length 10. Values 0-9 give digits, 10-35 give A-Z, 36-61 give a-z, 62-86 give the punctuation set '!@@$%^^*()_-+=[{]};:>|./?'. Required minimum of non-alphanumeric characters: 0.
edgeCases: Because 256 mod 87 is not 0, values 0-81 come up more often than 82-86 (slight bias)
'@' and '^' each appear twice in the punctuation set, so they are twice as likely
With a minimum of 0, the top-up loop never runs, so a password may contain no symbols

confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: There is no check that the user belongs to the target program. Whether access is blocked depends on FetchUserProgramPermissions returning nothing, which this code does not confirm.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should switching to a program the user is not assigned to be rejected outright? | Should the server reject a program id the user is not assigned to, rather than relying on the drop-down contents?

confirmedRules.name: Overridable warnings must be acknowledged before save
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Each broken rule is either a hard error that always blocks saving, or an overridable warning that blocks the first save attempt and lets the record through only after the user overrides it on a later attempt.
confirmedRules.given: A flight whose HobbsStart is 0, which raises overridable warning 02-00-011
confirmedRules.when: The user saves for the first time, then saves again after setting OverRideRule=True on that warning
confirmedRules.then: The first save fails and the warning goes into WarningsList. On the second save the earlier warning with the same RuleIdentifier is marked overridden, so it does not add to the error count and the save passes. Hard errors (OverRideableRule=False) always add to the error count and go into ErrorsList.

edgeCases: Matching uses RuleIdentifier alone, so warnings that share an ID (02-00-01B, and 02-00-20/21/22 across fluids) are overridden together
Rules built with the 2-argument constructor have an empty RuleIdentifier and are never overridable
If several earlier warnings share an ID, the same warning is added to WarningsList once per match, so it is duplicated
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Citation was corrected by referee (The cited lines, FLTBizObjects/BusinessObject/BrokenRule.vb:34-65, hold only the data carrier. They define the read-only OverRideableRule property (34-38), the OverRideRule setter that only takes a value when _overRideableRule is True (40-49), and two constructors (51-65). None of these lines count errors, block a save, or check earlier warnings. The behavior the rule describes is in FLTBizObjects/BusinessLogic/BrokenRuleManager.vb:8-37 (ConsiderRules). A broken rule that is not overridable adds 1 to the error count and goes into ErrorsList (lines 29-31). An overridable rule that was not in PrevWarningsList adds 1 and goes into WarningsList (lines 14-16). An overridable rule that was already in PrevWarningsList, where that earlier warning has the same RuleIdentifier and OverRideRule=True, is marked overridden and adds nothing to the count (lines 18-21). The callers, for example FLTBizObjects/BusinessObject/Aircraft.vb:903, pass validation only when ConsiderRules returns 0. One detail: the step that checks whether a warning existed before (lines 39-50) matches on PropertyName, RuleIdentifier and Message together, not on RuleIdentifier alone. I did not check the HobbsStart / 02-00-011 example, because it is outside the cited scope. The cited and surrounding code contains no instruction-shaped text.) — confirm FLTBizObjects/BusinessLogic/BrokenRuleManager.vb:8-37 is the authoritative implementation.

confirmedRules.name: Flight meter readings must run forward, and region time must add up to Hobbs usage
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A flight's ending Hobbs and ending engine hours cannot be lower than the starting values. When enabled, the hours split across regions must equal the flight's Hobbs usage (HobbsEnd - HobbsStart).
confirmedRules.given: A flight with HobbsStart 1,200.0, HobbsEnd 1,203.5 and region times 2.0 + 1.0
confirmedRules.when: The flight is validated with rule 02-00-01B enabled
confirmedRules.then: Hard error 'Total Region Usage of 3.0 doesn't match Flight Usage of 3.5' (02-00-01B). HobbsStart > HobbsEnd gives hard error 02-00-019. EngineHoursStart > EngineHoursEnd gives hard error 02-00-01A.
confirmedRules.parameters: Toggle: AppConfiguration.BusinessRuleEnabled("02-00-01B") (definition not found in the repo). Meter mask '#,##0.0;-#,##0.0'.
edgeCases: FlightRegionTime.Hours is a string formatted to 1 decimal place (FlightRegionTime.vb:79-92), so region hours are rounded to 0.1 before they are summed
The sum uses exact equality with no tolerance
Non-numeric region hours become 0
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The region sum adds strings formatted as '#,##0.0', so values rounded to 0.1 (or thousand separators that depend on culture) can cause false mismatches against unrounded Hobbs values.

confirmedRules.name: Flight start meters must continue from the aircraft's current meters
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A new flight's starting Hobbs (plus any meter offset) should equal the aircraft's current airframe hours, and its starting engine hours should equal the aircraft's current engine hours. Any difference raises an overridable warning.
confirmedRules.given: Aircraft airframe hours 1,500.0 and engine hours 800.0; a flight with HobbsStart 1,499.0, UsedMeterOffset 0 and EngineHoursStart 801.0
confirmedRules.then: Warning 02-00-1C 'Hobbs Start is less than aircraft's current meter' and warning 02-00-01X 'Start Engine Hours ... is greater than aircraft's current engine hours'. Both can be overridden.
confirmedRules.parameters: Comparison is HobbsStart + UsedMeterOffset vs AirframeHoursStart. Rule IDs: 02-00-01B (Hobbs greater), 02-00-1C (Hobbs less), 02-00-01X (engine greater), 02-00-01Y (engine less).
edgeCases: The engine 'greater than' check is skipped when the aircraft's current engine hours = 0, but the 'less than' check still runs
The Hobbs 'greater' warning reuses ID 02-00-01B, which is also the region-sum hard error
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Rule ID 02-00-01B is used both for the region-usage hard error and for this overridable warning, so an override can be matched to the wrong rule.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion:
P0 panel split on whether this is critical to the system's core purpose or a costly-if-wrong rule (The code at FLTBizObjects/BusinessObject/Flight.vb:1368-1390 matches the rule card. Engine hours: if EngineHoursStart is greater than the aircraft's current engine hours, the code raises 02-00-01X (line 1368). If it is less, it raises 02-00-01Y (line 1371). Hobbs: if HobbsStart + UsedMeterOffset is greater than AirframeHoursStart, it raises 02-00-01B (line 1385). If it is less, it raises 02-00-1C (line 1388). Every one of these BrokenRules is created with the overridable flag set to True. The worked example also checks out. 1,499 + 0 is less than 1,500, so 02-00-1C fires. 801 is greater than 800 and current engine hours are not zero, so 02-00-01X fires. Both can be overridden.

There are two small gaps that don't change the verdict. First, the 'greater' engine-hours check is skipped when the aircraft's current engine hours are 0 (`And _aircraftEngineHoursCurrent <> 0`). So 'any difference raises a warning' is not quite true, and the card should say so. Second, rule ID 02-00-01B is used twice: once here for the Hobbs check, and once in the region-hours mismatch check at lines 1375-1383, which a config switch can turn on or off. Only the region-hours use is gated by `BusinessRuleEnabled("02-00-01B")`; the Hobbs check at line 1385 always runs. Migration should not merge the two.

P0 check through the compliance lens: meter continuity does matter for keeping aircraft time records accurate, and those records feed maintenance-interval tracking and billing. But this code only warns. All four checks can be overridden and never block saving the flight. This is one of many similar warnings in the same validation routine (02-00-1E, 1F, 20, 21 and others), and it is not the system's central calculation. If it changed silently, the main loss would be a missing warning prompt, not a wrong recorded value. That is recoverable and not a regulatory control on its own. P1 (important data-quality warning) fits better than P0. I found no instruction-like text in the cited lines. | Fidelity: I checked the worked example against Flight.vb:1368-1390 and it holds. With _aircraftEngineHoursCurrent=800 (not 0), an EngineHoursStart of 801 hits line 1368 and produces 02-00-01X. HobbsStart 1499 plus offset 0 is less than _airframeHoursStart 1500, so line 1388 produces 02-00-1C. Both BrokenRules are built with the 4th argument True, which means overridable warnings. The rule IDs and the comparison (HobbsStart + UsedMeterOffset vs AirframeHoursStart) also match. There is no rounding: the values are plain Decimal comparisons. The card has three gaps to fix: (1) The plain-English claim that 'any difference raises a warning' is too strong. The engine-hours-greater check (line 1368) is skipped when the aircraft's current engine hours are 0, so an aircraft with no recorded engine hours never gets 02-00-01X. The engine-hours-less check (line 1371) has no such exemption. The Hobbs checks (1385/1388) have no zero exemption either. (2) Rule ID 02-00-01B is reused. At line 1381 it is a non-overridable region-hours-sum error, gated by AppConfiguration.BusinessRuleEnabled("02-00-01B"). At line 1386 it is the overridable Hobbs-greater warning, which is not gated. Using the ID to identify the rule in the new system is ambiguous. (3) The actual warning text reads 'engine hourss' (a typo in the code). Also, _airframeHoursStart and _aircraftEngineHoursCurrent are set to 0 when the input is null or invalid (lines 670-674, 769-773). So a missing aircraft meter value makes every non-zero Hobbs start warn 'greater'. P0: not justified. These checks only produce warnings the user can override (isWarning=True), so a user can always accept and save a gap. That makes this one of many soft validations, not the central decision or a hard integrity guard. The hard meter-integrity rules nearby, where end must be at least start (02-00-019 and 02-00-01A at lines 1360-1366), are non-overridable errors and are the better P0 candidates. Rate this one P1. No instruction-shaped text or credentials appear in the cited lines.) — confirm criticality.

confirmedRules.when: The values are assigned and Validate() runs (lines 878-906)

confirmedRules.then: Error 03-00-00D 'Please provide both Due Date and Due Time' is raised. With DueTime='14:30' or '2:30 PM' it passes; DueTime='25:00' raises 03-00-00C 'DueTime time format is invalid'
confirmedRules.parameters: TimeRegex (line 16): 12-hour h(:|.)mm with optional space and AM/PM in any case, or 24-hour H(:|.)mm with hours 0-23. Rule IDs 03-00-00B/03-00-00F (time required, unreachable), 03-00-00C DueTime format, 03-00-00D due pair, 03-00-010 FinishTime format

A period works as the separator ('14.30').

confirmedRules.then: FaultOccurredMeter displays '12,345.7' and FaultOccurredDate displays '' (blank)

edgeCases: Non-numeric FaultOccurredMeter input resets the reading to 0 (lines 222-226).

No rule checks MeterEndWork >= MeterStartWork, and no meter is required.
Display rounds to 1 decimal place but the full decimal value is stored.

confirmedRules.name: Work order aggregate validation rolls up all child lines
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A work order is valid only if its header and every attached reason, instruction, performed-work line, part, engineer comment and mechanic comment are valid. Every child error is added to the work order's error list.
confirmedRules.given: A work order with a valid header and one mechanic comment with CommentRating=0
confirmedRules.then: The mechanic comment's error 03-06-004 is added to the work order's BrokenRules and Validate returns False, which blocks the save
confirmedRules.parameters: All rules are created non-overridable, so BrokenRuleManager.ConsiderRules counts each one as a hard error and nothing is downgraded to an overridable warning
edgeCases: Child lines are validated even when flagged IsDeleted. Lines moved to the *DeleteList collections are not validated.
Document infos (WODocumentInfosList) are not validated.
Children get the work order's current _warningsList as their previous warnings. This has no effect today because no rule is overridable.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion:
P0 panel split on whether this is critical to the system's core purpose or a costly-if-wrong rule (The rule matches the code. In WorkOrder.vb:930-971, Validate loops over the reasons, instructions, performed-work lines, parts, engineer comments and mechanic comments. It calls each child's Validate and adds every child BrokenRule to Me.BrokenRules, which is the same list as _brokenRulesList (property at WorkOrder.vb:734-736). WOMechanicComment.vb:285-286 adds 03-06-004 when CommentRating is below 1 or above 10, so a rating of 0 triggers it. That rule, like the other child rules I found, is created with OverRideableRule=False. BrokenRuleManager.ConsiderRules (BusinessLogic/BrokenRuleManager.vb:8-36) counts any non-overridable rule as an error, so Validate returns False. WorkOrderManager.Update and Insert (WorkOrderManager.vb:44, 65) then throw "record is invalid" and nothing is saved. The Given/When/Then is accurate.

Through the compliance lens, P0 is not justified. This rule is a container that gathers up other field checks: required IDs, date and time formats, length limits, and a comment rating between 1 and 10. It is not a regulatory, financial or airworthiness decision in its own right. Aircraft maintenance records do matter to regulators, but a silent change here would let bad field values into child lines (for example a comment rating outside 1-10, or a comment that is too long). That is a data-quality problem, not a missing legally required record or a wrong maintenance decision. It is also partly backed up elsewhere: WorkOrderManager.InsertWOMechanicComment (WorkOrderManager.vb:408-409) and similar methods validate each child before adding it to the in-memory list. However, ProcessWOMechanicCommentList (WorkOrderManager.vb:764-778) saves children without validating them again, so this roll-up is the last check before saving. That makes it worth P1 coverage, with one equivalence test that a child error blocks the parent save, but it does not need to be part of the P0 behavior contract.

Side note for an SME: on a brand-new work order, child lines may not yet have a WorkOrderId, so rule 03-06-001 might fire and block the insert. I did not confirm this. I found no instruction-like text in the cited lines. | The card matches the code. I checked it line by line. WorkOrder.vb:930-971 goes through six child collections in order: WOReasonList, WOInstructionList, WOPerformedWorkList, WOPartList, WOEngineerCommentList and WOMechanicCommentList. It calls Validate(_warningsList) on each child. When a child returns False, its BrokenRules are appended to Me.BrokenRules, and that property returns the header's own _brokenRulesList (WorkOrder.vb:734-738). Lines 973-976 then reset _errorsList and _warningsList and return ConsiderRules(...) = 0. The Given/When/Then example holds. WOMechanicComment.vb:285-287 adds 03-06-004 when _commentRating < 1 or > 10, so a rating of 0 triggers it. The comment's own ConsiderRules (WOMechanicComment.vb:310) then returns False, so the rule is copied to the work order. The rule is built with OverRideableRule=False (BrokenRule.vb:59-65), so ConsiderRules (BrokenRuleManager.vb:29-31) counts it as an error and the work order's Validate returns False. The save is blocked because WorkOrderManager.vb:44 and :65 only save when WorkOrder.Validate() is True. The claim that every rule is non-overridable also holds: grep found no BrokenRule built with True in WorkOrder, WO*.vb or WorkOrderPart. Small edge cases the card leaves out, for the equivalence contract: (1) a child's rules are copied only when that child's Validate returns False, so a child that passes adds nothing; (2) the children get the _warningsList field rather than the WarningsList argument, which only matters for overridable rules, and there are none today; (3) child rules are added after the header rules, with no de-duplication, so the order is header rules first, then children in the six-collection order above. A note on 03-06-006 and 03-06-007: these mechanic-comment rules only apply when AppConfiguration.BusinessRuleEnabled is on, so some child rules depend on configuration. None of these points makes the card wrong. P0: justified, though only just. Each child check is an ordinary validation, but this roll-up is the integrity rule for the whole work order. It is the only thing that stops a maintenance work order being saved with invalid child lines. Aircraft maintenance records relate to safety and airworthiness. If a rewrite drops or weakens this roll-up, every child validation would silently stop blocking saves. That makes it a reasonable item for the behavior contract. No instruction-like text was found in the cited lines.) — confirm criticality.

confirmedRules.given: A part line with PartName='Fuel pump', FisIDRemoved='FIS-0042', FisIDAdded=''
confirmedRules.then: Error 03-05-007 'FisIDAdded is required' is raised
confirmedRules.parameters: PartName required (03-05-002), max 20 (03-05-003); PartDescription max 255 (also tagged 03-05-003); FisIDRemoved required when 03-05-004 is on, max 20 (03-05-005); FisIDAdded required when 03-05-007 is on, max 20 (03-05-008); PartModule max 20 (03-05-009)
edgeCases: The FIS-ID requirements can be switched off, but the 20-character limits always apply.
The PartDescription length error reuses rule ID 03-05-003, the same ID as the PartName length rule.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The PartDescription length rule reuses ID 03-05-003, so the two rules cannot be told apart when reporting or overriding.

confirmedRules.name: Part quantities must be whole numbers 0-999
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The number of parts failed, removed and added must each be a whole number of 1 to 3 digits (0-999). Each defaults to 0.
confirmedRules.given: A part line with PartNbrRemoved='2', PartNbrAdded='1000', PartNbrFailed='1.5'
confirmedRules.then: PartNbrRemoved passes. PartNbrAdded fails with 03-05-00E 'must be a number'. PartNbrFailed fails with 03-05-00C
confirmedRules.parameters: WholeNumberRegExMask '^\d{1,3}$' (line 15); defaults '0' (lines 103-166). Switch keys 03-05-00C (failed), 03-05-00D (removed), 03-05-00E (added); 'required' messages carry IDs 03-05-006, 03-05-00A, 03-05-00B
edgeCases: The 'required' branches cannot fire: the setters turn Nothing into '0', and VB string '=' Nothing also matches ''.
Negative numbers and leading '+' are rejected; '007' is accepted.
Nothing checks that removed equals added or that failed is at most removed.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Each 'required' message carries a different rule ID (03-05-006/00A/00B) from the switch that controls it (03-05-00C/00D/00E). Turning off 03-05-006 has no effect.

confirmedRules.name: Work order record lifecycle (new, edit, soft delete, concurrency)
confirmedRules.source: FLTBizObjects/BusinessLogic/WorkOrderManager.vb:118-122 (temporary negative IDs), FLTBizObjects/BusinessLogic/WorkOrderManager.vb:312-318 (moving removed parts to WOPartDeleteList), FLTBizObjects/DataAccess/WorkOrderDB.vb:528-536 (processing the delete list via WorkOrderPartDB.Delete; soft delete not confirmed), FLTBizObjects/BusinessObject/WorkOrder.vb:752-817 (default values only)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A new work order is marked by ID -1 and concurrency token '0'. Child lines being added get temporary negative IDs, removed child lines go into delete lists, and records are deleted by setting the IsDeleted flag instead of being removed.
confirmedRules.given: A user creates a new work order and adds a reason line, then removes a different existing part line
confirmedRules.when: The object graph is built for save
confirmedRules.then: WorkOrderId=-1, ConcurrencyId='0', NewWoReasonId starts at -1 as the temporary key, the removed part goes to WOPartDeleteList, and IsDeleted marks deleted records
confirmedRules.parameters: New-record sentinel WorkOrderId=-1; ConcurrencyId initial '0' (optimistic concurrency token); temporary child IDs start at -1; IsDeleted default False; audit fields UtcDateCreated, UtcDateModified, StampUserName
edgeCases: The child classes start with ID 0, not -1.
The _nextWO*LineNbr fields (lines 60-84) are declared but never used in this file, so line numbering is assigned elsewhere.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Where are the concurrency check, temporary-ID resolution and soft-delete persistence enforced (DAL or stored procedures), and are deleted work orders ever purged under a retention rule?

confirmedRules.name: Work order status has no enforced transitions in the business object
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A work order must have a status, but this object accepts any status ID and any change between statuses, and does not tie finish date/time or engineering action to a particular status.
confirmedRules.given: A work order with WorkOrderStatusId changed from 1 to any other non-zero ID and no FinishDate
confirmedRules.then: The work order is valid. No transition, completion-date or sign-off check is applied
confirmedRules.parameters: Only check: WorkOrderStatusId != 0 (03-00-005). The status lookup values are not defined in these files
edgeCases: A finish date can be entered while the status is still open, and a closed status can be saved without a finish date.
AircraftIssueAlert and MaintIssueAlert are free flags with no rule.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: What are the work order statuses (e.g. Open, In Work, Closed) and their allowed transitions? Must a finish date/time, end meter or mechanic be present before a work order can be closed, and is that enforced in the UI or stored procedures?

confirmedRules.name: Weight definition required fields and description charset
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A weight definition must belong to a program and have a weight tracking type, a description using only allowed characters, a non-zero weight and a weight unit.
confirmedRules.given: A weight definition with ProgId=12, WeightDefTypeId=3, WeightDefDescr='Max Takeoff (MTOW)', Weight='79,000', WeightUnitId=1
confirmedRules.then: It passes and Weight displays as '79,000'. With Weight='abc' the weight becomes 0 and 'Weight value is required' is raised
confirmedRules.parameters: Common-string regex default '^([A-Za-z0-9 .#\/()_-])*$' (ObjectPropertyValidator.vb:101-113, can be changed with appSetting CommonRegEx); weight stored as Integer via CInt; display '#,##0'; IsActive defaults True
edgeCases: A decimal weight is rounded by CInt using banker's rounding ('2.5' becomes 2, '3.5' becomes 4).
Negative weights pass because only 0 is rejected.
The default error text says only letters, numbers, spaces, periods, dashes, underscores and slashes are allowed, but the regex also allows '#' and parentheses.
None of these rule messages has a rule ID.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Negative weights are accepted, and decimal weights are silently rounded to an integer.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should negative or zero weights be valid for any weight tracking type, and are there per-type limits on weight values?

confirmedRules.name: Weight tracking type description rule
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A weight tracking type must have a description, and the description may contain only the common allowed characters.
confirmedRules.given: A WeightDefType with WeightDefTypeDescr='Fuel*Load'
confirmedRules.then: The error 'WeightDefTypeDescr should only contain letters, numbers, ...' is raised because '*' is not allowed
confirmedRules.parameters: Same common-string regex as WeightDef
edgeCases: The 'required' message has a typo: 'WeightDefTyepDescr'.

confirmedRules.name: User session authorization context defaults to no access
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A user session starts as not logged in, not a super user and not a program manager, with no programs and no module permissions. Access is denied until rights are loaded, and per-module rights are View and Edit flags that default to false.
confirmedRules.given: An anonymous visitor
confirmedRules.then: IsLoggedIn=False, UserDisplayName='Unknown', IsSuperUser=False, CurrentProgId=0, IsCurrentProgramManager=False, and the program and permission lists are empty
confirmedRules.parameters: UserModulePermissions(ModuleName, CanView=False, CanEdit=False) defaults (lines 92-96); roles: super user, current-program manager
edgeCases: The parameterized constructor accepts ProgDisplayName but never assigns it, so the display name stays blank.
The constructor initializes _userProgramsList twice (harmless).
This class only holds the flags. The decisions that use them are made elsewhere.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: What can a super user or program manager do that a normal user cannot, and does Edit permission imply View permission?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The ProgDisplayName constructor argument is silently ignored (line 186 vs 187-196).

confirmedRules.name: Fixed catalog of administrator-maintainable lookup (configuration value) types
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Administrators can maintain configuration values only for a fixed, hardcoded list of 26 lookup types (for example Pilot, Mechanic, Engine Type, Work Order Status, Work Order Type, Aircraft Status), offered in that order.
confirmedRules.given: An administrator opens the Config Values maintenance screen (FLTWebApp/program/ConfigValues.aspx.vb:144-149) or the Config Values report (FLTWebApp/reports/rptConfigValues.aspx.vb:74)
confirmedRules.when: The lookup Type drop-down is populated
confirmedRules.then: It shows exactly these 26 types, in this order: APUType, Pilot, Emission, Engineer, EngineeringAction, EngineType, IssueCode, LengthUnit, LiquidGroup, LiquidType, LiquidUnit, Manufacturer, MaturityDef, MechAction, Model, Mechanic, Test, LoadingConfig, Propeller, PropellerType, AircraftComponent, AircraftStatusDef, WeightUnit, WorkOrderStatus, WorkOrderType, WorkShift. No other lookup type can be picked from the UI.
confirmedRules.parameters: 26 hardcoded lookup type names (lines 13-38). These are a good candidate for configuration or a database reference table. Per the step 01 map, each name is also joined to a stored procedure prefix ("fetch" & LookupName), so each entry implies a matching stored procedure.
edgeCases: The list is not alphabetical: Mechanic comes after Model, and Test, LoadingConfig, Propeller and the rest are appended after it. The modern system should keep this display order or deliberately decide to change it.
Values such as WorkOrderStatus and AircraftStatusDef make lifecycle states (work order status, aircraft status) data an administrator maintains, not states fixed in code.
Adding a new lookup type needs a code change here plus a matching stored procedure.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is this the complete, authoritative set of lookup types administrators may maintain? Are any intentionally left out (for example WeightDefType, WOReason, WOPerformedWork) because they are managed elsewhere, and does the display order matter to users?

confirmedRules.name: Takeoff weight defaults to sum of component weights
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: If a flight has no stored takeoff weight, or its stored takeoff weight is zero, the system uses airframe + cargo 1 + cargo 2 + ballast weight.
confirmedRules.given: A flight whose stored TakeoffWeight is NULL or 0, with AirframeWeight 9,000, Cargo1Weight 500, Cargo2Weight 250 and BallastWeight 100
confirmedRules.then: TakeoffWeight = 9,000 + 500 + 250 + 100 = 9,850. A non-zero stored TakeoffWeight is used as stored.
confirmedRules.parameters: Inputs are AirframeWeight, Cargo1Weight, Cargo2Weight and BallastWeight. Each is an integer that comes from a weight lookup row (AirframeWeightId and so on, lines 501-563). A NULL component counts as 0.
edgeCases: A missing weight component is treated as 0 in the sum
An explicit takeoff weight of 0 cannot be stored: it is always replaced by the computed sum
Weight units (AirframeWeightUnit and the others) are not checked or converted before summing
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The sum adds weights without checking that they share a unit, even though each component has its own unit field. If a flight mixes units, its takeoff weight is wrong.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion:
P0 panel split on whether this is critical to the system's core purpose or a costly-if-wrong rule (The card matches the code. In FLTBizObjects/DataAccess/FlightDB.vb:565-570, a non-NULL stored TakeoffWeight is assigned first. If the result is still 0 (NULL, or a stored 0), it is replaced with AirframeWeight + Cargo1Weight + Cargo2Weight + BallastWeight. A NULL component counts as 0 in two places: fetchFlight wraps each weight in ISNULL(...,0) (database/FLT_Schema.sql:8686-8700), and the VB property setters turn Nothing into 0 (FLTBizObjects/BusinessObject/Flight.vb:290-298). So 9,000+500+250+100 = 9,850 is correct.

Points to carry into the card:
(1) fetchFlight returns Flight.* plus a second column also named TakeoffWeight, which is always the computed sum (FLT_Schema.sql:8686). GetOrdinal returns the first match, which is the stored column, so the code works as the card says. A rewrite that maps columns by name or ORM could silently pick the other column, so this needs an equivalence test.
(2) FlightDB's save paths never write TakeoffWeight (no @TakeoffWeight parameter near lines 190-197 and 370). The derived value is display and export only, and it is never saved back.

Why P0 holds under the compliance lens: this is an aviation flight log for instrumented aircraft (pre-flight FTI and telemetry checks, approvals). Takeoff weight is a weight-and-balance figure an airworthiness auditor or flight-test authority would expect to be accurate. It is shown on FlightModify (FLTWebApp/fleet/FlightModify.aspx.vb:393) and written to the XML export (FLTBizObjects/BusinessLogic/FltExportManager.vb:333). If this changed silently, for example 0 shown instead of the sum or a stale stored value used, the safety record would be wrong and the error would leave the system through the export. The rule is a derivation and fallback, not a limit check. It earns P0 on safety and data integrity, not because it is the system's central calculation. SME question: should a stored 0 really mean 'not entered', or can an operator legitimately record 0?

No instruction-like text was found in the cited lines. | Fidelity: the rule matches the code. In FlightDB.vb:565-567 the stored TakeoffWeight is read only when it is not DBNull. Lines 568-570 then replace a value of 0 with AirframeWeight + Cargo1Weight + Cargo2Weight + BallastWeight. The weights are plain integers, so no rounding happens. The example (9,000 + 500 + 250 + 100 = 9,850) is correct. "A NULL component counts as 0" also holds: fetchFlight wraps each component in ISNULL(...,0) (FLT_Schema.sql:8687-8700), FillDataRecord skips DBNull, and the Integer fields in Flight.vb default to 0. A non-zero stored value is kept as stored. Two edge cases are missing from the card. (1) fetchFlight (FLT_Schema.sql:8680-8686) returns [Flight].* plus a second column also named TakeoffWeight, which the procedure itself computes as the same ISNULL sum. GetOrdinal returns the first matching column, which is the stored column, so the VB fallback is what actually takes effect. But the SQL repeats the same rule, and a rewrite must not get confused by the duplicate name. (2) addFlight/updateFlight never send a TakeoffWeight parameter: "Takeoff" appears in FlightDB.vb only at lines 565-569, and the column defaults to 0 (FLT_Schema.sql:1688). So for flights the app creates, the computed sum is effectively always used, and the "stored value" path only matters for seeded or legacy rows. If all four components are 0 or missing, the result stays 0. Priority: P0 is not justified. Takeoff weight is relevant to safety, but here it is only a value worked out when the record loads. It is shown on the flight edit page (FlightModify.aspx.vb:393) and written to the XML export (FltExportManager.vb:333). No limit check, approval, or other decision depends on it, and nothing is saved back. It is one derived display/export field in a flight-logging system, not the system's central decision. P1 fits better, with an equivalence test that covers the duplicate-column behavior. I found no instruction-like text in the lines cited.) — confirm criticality.

confirmedRules.name: Flight log saved as one atomic unit with its child records
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A flight and its liquid fills, pilot comments, engine runs and region times are all saved, or none are. Each child is inserted if it is new or updated if it already exists, and removed children are deleted only if they were ever saved.
confirmedRules.given: A flight with one new liquid fill (no ConcurrencyId), one edited engine run (with a ConcurrencyId) and one region time on the delete list with Id 42
confirmedRules.then: In one transaction: the flight is updated, the liquid fill is inserted, the engine run is updated and region time 42 is deleted. If any step fails, everything is rolled back. Each child gets the parent's FlightId and StampUserName.
confirmedRules.parameters: A child is treated as new when its ConcurrencyId is Nothing, empty or "0" (lines 630-740). A child on a delete list is deleted only when its Id is > 0.
edgeCases: On insert of a new flight, only the add lists are processed. Delete lists are ignored (lines 286-344).
Children on a delete list that were never saved (Id 0) are dropped silently
The audit user on every child is overwritten with the parent flight's StampUserName

confirmedRules.name: Duplicate flight entries are rejected
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A new flight that the database flags as a duplicate is rejected with the message that this flight already exists.
confirmedRules.given: A flight entry that duplicates an existing one, by whatever key the addFlight procedure enforces
confirmedRules.when: The user saves it as a new flight
confirmedRules.then: The save fails with 'Can't insert - this flight already exists in the database.' and the whole transaction, including children, is rolled back
confirmedRules.parameters: Database error text matched: "Duplicate Flight Entry". Message shown to the user: "Can't insert - this flight already exists in the database."
edgeCases: The duplicate check itself lives in the addFlight stored procedure, not in this code
Any other insert error becomes the generic 'Application encountered a data error.'
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Which fields define a duplicate flight in the addFlight stored procedure (for example aircraft + flight date + departure time, or the FlightGuid)?

confirmedRules.name: Optimistic concurrency on record updates
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A record can be updated only if nobody else changed it since it was read. Otherwise the user sees 'Row has been edited by another user'.
confirmedRules.given: User A and user B both open flight 100 with row version X, and B saves first, so the row version becomes Y
confirmedRules.when: User A saves flight 100 still holding version X
confirmedRules.then: The update is rejected with 'Row has been edited by another user' and A's whole save transaction rolls back
confirmedRules.parameters: The row version (SQL timestamp) is sent as @ConcurrencyId and the new one is returned in @NewConcurrencyId. The same pattern applies in AircraftDB.vb:243-249, FltUserDB.vb and the other updates in this module.
edgeCases: Only this exact message is passed through to the user. Other SQL errors are hidden behind a generic message.
Rows with no row version are inserted, not updated

confirmedRules.name: Flight approval state is recorded with approver and timestamp
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A flight has an approval state: an approved flag, who approved it and the UTC approval time. The aircraft view lists only flights that are approved, active and not deleted.
confirmedRules.given: Aircraft 7 has three flights: one approved and active, one not yet approved, and one approved but soft-deleted
confirmedRules.then: Only the approved, active, non-deleted flight appears in the aircraft's flight list
confirmedRules.parameters: IsApproved (bit), ApprovedBy (nvarchar 20), UTCDateApproved (datetime). AircraftDB.vb:39 calls FlightInfoDB.GetList with IsApprovedFilter=1, IsActiveFilter=1, IsDeletedFilter=0.
edgeCases: NULL approval columns load as not approved (FlightDB.vb:607-615)
The data layer does not enforce who may approve or require ApprovedBy when IsApproved is true
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should flights that are not yet approved really be hidden from the aircraft detail view? And which role may set IsApproved, and can approval be reversed?

confirmedRules.name: Soft-delete and active filtering when loading flight and aircraft details
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Deletes are soft: records carry IsDeleted and IsActive flags. Detail views load only active, non-deleted child records, except engine runs, which are filtered only on not deleted.
confirmedRules.given: Flight 100 has an inactive liquid fill, a deleted pilot comment and an inactive engine run
confirmedRules.then: The inactive liquid fill and the deleted comment are excluded. The inactive engine run is still shown.
confirmedRules.parameters: LiquidFill: IsActive=1 and IsDeleted=0. FlightComment: active=1, deleted=0. FlightRegionTime: active=1, deleted=0. FlightEngineRun: only IsDeleted=0. Aircraft (AircraftDB.vb:35-36): configurations IsDeleted=0, locations active=1 and deleted=0. Every delete procedure records StampUserName.
edgeCases: Engine runs have no active filter, unlike the other flight children
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is it intended that inactive engine runs appear on a flight while inactive fills, comments and region times are hidden?

confirmedRules.name: Only aircraft comments can be added from the aircraft record
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The aircraft screen shows one combined comment list (aircraft, flight, work-order engineer and mechanic comments). Only aircraft comments can be created there. Existing comments of the other types can be edited, and unknown comment types are rejected.
confirmedRules.given: An aircraft save with changed comments: a new aircraft comment, an edited flight comment and a new work-order engineer comment
confirmedRules.then: The aircraft comment is inserted and the flight comment is updated. The new engineer comment fails with 'Adding a comment that is not an Aircraft Comment is not allowed', and the whole aircraft save rolls back.
confirmedRules.parameters: Source types: AircraftComment, FlightComment, WOEngineerComment, WOMechanicComment. A comment counts as new when its ConcurrencyId is Nothing or "0". Only comments with IsDirty=True are processed (loaded comments start with IsDirty=False, GenericCommentDB.vb:142).
edgeCases: Any other SourceTable value fails with 'Unknown Comment Type'
Flight comments edited from here are forced to IsActive=True (line 668)
On aircraft comments, the comment AuthorID becomes EngineerId (line 639)
On delete, only AircraftComment rows with SourceID > 0 are deleted. Other comment types on the delete list are ignored silently (lines 583-589).
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Aircraft comment deletes (line 586) and aircraft location deletes (line 530) use the overloads that open their own connection, not the aircraft save transaction. They are committed even if the aircraft save later rolls back. _sortGenericCommentList (lines 613-633, newest first by CommentDate) is defined but never called.

confirmedRules.name: Aircraft test assignments are added only once
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When an aircraft is saved, each test on its test list is linked to the aircraft only if that link does not already exist. Tests on the remove list are unlinked.
confirmedRules.given: Aircraft 7 is already linked to test 3, and its test list contains tests 3 and 5
confirmedRules.then: Only the link to test 5 is created. Test 3 is left unchanged.
confirmedRules.parameters: Existence check: existsAircraftTestXref returns @Exists (AircraftTestXrefDB.vb:385-417). The list of tests available to an aircraft is scoped by program (ProgId, AircraftTestXrefDB.vb:64-75).
edgeCases: Deletes are run for every test on the remove list, with no existence check
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The Exists, Insert (3-argument) and Delete (3-argument) calls each open their own connection or transaction rather than using the aircraft save transaction (Conn/Trans are passed in but not used). Test link changes therefore survive a rollback of the aircraft save.

confirmedRules.name: Aircraft save is atomic with its configurations and locations
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Saving an aircraft also saves its configuration history, location history, comments and test links in one transaction. New child rows are inserted, existing ones are updated, and removed ones are deleted only if they were ever saved.
confirmedRules.given: Aircraft 7 with a new configuration (no ConcurrencyId), an edited location, and a configuration with Id 12 on the delete list
confirmedRules.then: The aircraft is updated, the new configuration is inserted, the location is updated and configuration 12 is deleted. Every child gets AircraftId=7 and the aircraft's StampUserName.
confirmedRules.parameters: A child is new when its ConcurrencyId is Nothing or "0" (lines 488 and 516). A child on a delete list is deleted only when its Id is > 0.
edgeCases: On insert of a new aircraft, delete lists are not processed (lines 257-316)
AircraftDB.GetItem does not roll back on errors while loading children (lines 43-49)
The aircraft record carries AircraftStatusId, but no status transitions are enforced in this layer
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Which aircraft status values exist, and which transitions are allowed? They are not enforced in the data layer.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: See the comment, location and test rules: some child deletes or inserts run outside this transaction.

confirmedRules.name: Optional test-end and arrival dates are stored only when they are valid dates
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: An aircraft's estimated and actual end-of-testing dates are optional. A blank or invalid value is stored as empty (NULL) and does not cause an error.
confirmedRules.given: An aircraft with EstEndOfTesting '06-30-2026' and ActEndOfTesting ''
confirmedRules.then: EstEndOfTesting is stored as 2026-06-30 and ActEndOfTesting is stored as NULL
confirmedRules.parameters: Dates are checked with IsDate and loaded back in MM-dd-yyyy format. Configuration start and end dates are sent as Nothing when empty (AircraftConfigurationDB.vb:210-220).
edgeCases: AircraftLocationDB.vb:213-227: when ArrivalDate, EstEndOfTest or ActEndOfTest is not a valid date, the parameter value is left unset instead of DBNull
AircraftLocation EstEndOfTest and ActEndOfTest are passed as the raw string, not CDate
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should an aircraft location with no arrival date be saveable? Today the parameter is left unset, which the stored procedure may reject.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: In AircraftLocationDB.Update and Insert, invalid or blank dates leave the SqlParameter Value as Nothing rather than DBNull.Value. ADO.NET then omits the parameter, so the call may fail unless the procedure has a default.

confirmedRules.name: Meter, hour and liquid readings are rounded to fixed precision
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Hobbs, airframe-hours, engine-hours and meter offset readings are handled at one decimal place. Liquid amounts use three decimals. Because the formatted value is what gets saved back, a load-and-save cycle stores values at that precision.
confirmedRules.given: A flight whose HobbsEnd is stored as 1234.56
confirmedRules.when: The flight is loaded and saved again
confirmedRules.then: HobbsEnd is shown as '1,234.6' and saved back as 1234.6
confirmedRules.parameters: Hours, Hobbs, meter offset, region hours and required/accumulated usage use format #,##0.0. LiquidAmt uses #,##0.000 (LiquidFillDB.vb:415). Values are converted back to numbers with CDec on save.
edgeCases: Any extra precision held in the database is lost on the first edit
Thousands separators and locale settings affect the CDec conversion back
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is one decimal place (0.1 hour) the official precision for Hobbs, airframe and engine hours, and three decimals for liquid fills?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Formatting for display is used as the in-memory value, so a load-and-save cycle silently rounds stored readings.

confirmedRules.name: Login lockout thresholds
