confirmedRules.plainEnglish: An account locks after a set number of failed logins (default 3) and stays locked for a set number of minutes (default 5). Both values can be configured.
confirmedRules.given: No LockoutDuration or MaximumLoginFailuresAllowed in app settings
confirmedRules.when: A user fails to log in repeatedly
confirmedRules.then: The limit is 3 failures and the lockout lasts 5 minutes from the start of the failed-attempt window (applied in BusinessLogic/fltIdentityManager.vb:37-51)
confirmedRules.parameters: LockoutDuration defaults to 5 (minutes). MaximumLoginFailuresAllowed defaults to 3. A setting that is not numeric falls back to the default.
edgeCases: The failed-attempt count and window start are kept on the user record (FltUserDB.vb:147-153)
The lockout check in fltIdentityManager compares the attempt count against MaximumLoginFailuresAllowed - 1
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Confirm that the lockout should last 5 minutes measured from the start of the failed-attempt window (not from the last failure), and that the 3rd failed attempt is the one that locks the account.

confirmedRules.name: User account dates before 1800 are treated as not set
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Any user date (last login, last lockout, last password change, failed-attempt window starts) earlier than year 1800 is treated as never set and saved as empty.
confirmedRules.given: A new user whose UtcLastLockoutDate is the default 0001-01-01
confirmedRules.then: UtcLastLockoutDate is sent as empty (Nothing) rather than 0001-01-01
confirmedRules.parameters: Cutoff year: 1800
edgeCases: The value is sent as Nothing rather than DBNull.Value, so the parameter may be omitted
FltUserDB.Insert does not pass IsActive (lines 206-268), so the database default applies
Password, salt and security answer are stored as given; any hashing happens upstream
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Are passwords and security answers hashed before they reach FltUserDB, and what IsActive default does addFltUser apply?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Using Nothing instead of DBNull.Value may make the update procedure fail with a 'parameter not supplied' error if it has no default.

confirmedRules.name: Documents are stored in fixed-size chunks
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: An uploaded document is saved as an empty stub record, then its content is appended in chunks whose size is set by the FileBufferSize setting.
confirmedRules.given: FileBufferSize = 8192 and a 20,000-byte upload
confirmedRules.then: Chunks of 8,192, 8,192 and 3,616 bytes are appended at offsets 0, 8192 and 16384
confirmedRules.parameters: FileBufferSize comes from app settings and has no default. Stored procedures: addDocument, then appendDocumentChunk.
edgeCases: If FileBufferSize is missing, the conversion fails and the upload errors
The stub and chunks are not wrapped in a transaction, so a failure part-way leaves a partial document
On read, the content is limited to DocumentSize bytes (lines 131-168)
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is a partially stored document acceptable after an upload fails, or should the upload be all-or-nothing?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Uploads are not transactional, and a missing FileBufferSize setting breaks both upload and download.

confirmedRules.name: Linking documents to work orders
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Documents are attached to and detached from work orders through a link record. The system can check whether a given link already exists.
confirmedRules.given: Document 9 and work order 55
confirmedRules.when: The document is attached, checked and later detached
confirmedRules.then: addWorkOrderDocXref creates the link, existsWorkOrderDocXref returns true, and deleteWorkOrderDocXref removes the link, recording the acting user
confirmedRules.parameters: Stored procedures: addWorkOrderDocXref, existsWorkOrderDocXref, deleteWorkOrderDocXref
edgeCases: The inner Delete overload never sets myDbCommand.Transaction even though the caller opened a transaction
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Which records should 'work orders for a document' return? The current code calls the documents-for-work-order procedure with the DocumentId passed as WorkOrderId.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: ListWorkOrderInfosForDocument (lines 148-160) calls listDocumentInfosForWorkOrder and passes DocumentId as @WorkOrderId, so it returns the wrong data. Delete (lines 300-318) runs on a connection with an open transaction without attaching that transaction, which ADO.NET rejects at run time.

confirmedRules.name: Work order and all its child records are saved as one all-or-nothing unit
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When a work order is saved, the header and every attached reason, instruction, performed-work line, part, engineer comment, mechanic comment and document link are written in a single transaction; if any piece fails, nothing is saved.
confirmedRules.given: An existing work order #1001 with 2 new reasons, 1 edited instruction, 1 part marked for removal and 1 attached document
confirmedRules.when: The user saves the work order and the part-removal step fails in the database
confirmedRules.then: The whole save is rolled back: header changes, new reasons and the edited instruction are not persisted, and the user sees either the concurrency message or 'Application encountered a data error.'
confirmedRules.parameters: Processing order on update: header (updateWorkOrder) -> reasons upsert -> reasons delete -> instructions upsert/delete -> performed work upsert/delete -> parts upsert/delete -> engineer comments upsert/delete -> mechanic comments upsert/delete -> documents link/unlink -> commit. On insert (lines 238-303) the header is created first (addWorkOrder returns the new WorkOrderId), each child is stamped with that id, and delete lists are NOT processed.
edgeCases: On a new work order, delete lists are ignored entirely (lines 256-268)
Every child inherits the parent's StampUserName and WorkOrderId before being saved (lines 431-432 etc.)
Work order number (WorkOrderNbr) is never sent on insert; it is read back from the database, so numbering is assigned by the database (line 386)
GetItem (lines 15-72) also loads header plus all six child lists and document infos in one transaction
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: _processWODocumentInfosList calls DocumentInfoDB.Update(thisDocumentInfo) without passing the open connection/transaction (line 600), so document metadata updates are committed independently and are not rolled back if the rest of the work order save fails.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion:
P0 panel doubts spec fidelity: P0 is justified. This is the persistence contract for aircraft maintenance work orders. A partial save would leave a work order out of step with the parts, performed work and comments recorded against it, which is an aviation-safety and data-integrity problem. Every rewrite has to preserve this behavior.

The rule is not fully faithful, though. Parts of it are confirmed:
- Update (WorkOrderDB.vb:113-180) opens one connection and one SqlTransaction.
- It runs the steps in the stated order: _update, then each upsert list followed by its delete list for reasons, instructions, performed work, parts, engineer comments, mechanic comments and documents, then Commit.
- Any exception rolls the transaction back (lines 151-158).
- Insert (238-303) runs _insert first, stamps the new WorkOrderId (line 254), processes only the upsert lists with no delete lists, and then commits.
- The scenario's outcome holds as well: the part-delete step uses the transaction-bound WorkOrderPartDB.Delete overload (WorkOrderPartDB.vb:361). It fails before document processing begins, so the header, reasons and instructions are rolled back.

Fidelity defects:

(1) The headline overclaims. The rule says every document link is written in the same all-or-nothing transaction. In _processWODocumentInfosList (WorkOrderDB.vb:596-608), DocumentInfoDB.Update(thisDocumentInfo) is called without the connection or transaction; it opens its own connection (DocumentInfoDB.vb:112-120). DocumentWorkOrderXrefDB.Exists (DocumentWorkOrderXrefDB.vb:319) also runs outside the transaction. So document metadata updates commit on their own and are not rolled back if a later step (the document-unlink delete list) or the commit fails. Only the xref Insert and Delete calls are transactional. The rule also says "document link/unlink" but leaves out the out-of-transaction metadata update.

(2) The error message is not "either/or". Every child processor (for example _processWOPartDeleteList at lines 528-538) catches and rethrows as a plain System.Exception, not an ApplicationException. That routes it to the generic catch at line 155, so a part-removal failure always shows "Application encountered a data error." The concurrency text "Row has been edited by another user" can only come from the header step, _update (lines 225-226).

(3) Side note, a possible SME or build question: the Finally blocks test myDbConn.Region = ConnectionState.Open (lines 172 and 293). SqlConnection has no Region property; the expected property is State. The same pattern appears across the DataAccess folder. It is not instruction-shaped text, but it should be confirmed against the build.

No prompt-injection text was found in the cited lines.

confirmedRules.name: Optimistic concurrency: reject a save when someone else edited the record first
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Every update sends the record's version stamp as last read; if the database reports the row was changed by another user since then, the save is refused and the user is told 'Row has been edited by another user'.
confirmedRules.given: Two planners open work order #1001 with version stamp 7209; planner A saves first, moving the stamp to 7210
confirmedRules.when: Planner B saves the copy still carrying stamp 7209
confirmedRules.then: The update procedure raises 'Row has been edited by another user', the DAL surfaces that exact message to the user (not the generic data-error text), and for a work order the whole transaction is rolled back
confirmedRules.parameters: Exact match string: "Row has been edited by another user" (raised by stored procedures, matched by message text). Applied identically in ProgramDB.vb:153-159, RouteDB.vb:141-147, RegionDB.vb:134-140, UTCTimeZoneDB.vb:151-157, WeightDefDB.vb:141-147, WeightDefTypeDB.vb:132, fltLookupBaseDb.vb:133-139, WorkOrderPartDB.vb:225-231, WOEngineerCommentDB.vb:224-230, WOMechanicCommentDB.vb:225, WOReasonDB.vb:217, WOInstructionDB.vb:217, WOPerformedWorkDB.vb:217.
edgeCases: Inserts do not carry a version stamp and cannot conflict
The conflict check itself lives in the stored procedures; the code relies on an exact English error message

In the standalone child-record Update wrappers (e.g. WorkOrderPartDB.vb:166-168, WOEngineerCommentDB.vb:165-167) the concurrency message is swallowed and replaced with the generic data-error text, so the user cannot tell a conflict from a failure
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should child-record edits saved on their own (outside the work-order save) also show the 'edited by another user' message? Today those wrappers hide it. | Is ConcurrencyId a SQL Server rowversion/timestamp column (changes automatically), or does a trigger or the application increment it? If neither, the second save would succeed and the check would not work.

confirmedRules.name: Child record insert-vs-update decided by presence of a version stamp; deletes only for saved rows
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A work-order child line with no version stamp (empty or "0") is treated as new and inserted; one with a stamp is updated; lines in the delete list are removed only if they already have a database id greater than zero.
confirmedRules.given: A work order with reason line A (ConcurrencyId empty), reason line B (ConcurrencyId "7209"), and a delete list holding reason C (WOReasonId 0) and reason D (WOReasonId 55)
confirmedRules.then: A is inserted, B is updated, C is ignored (never saved so nothing to delete), and D is deleted stamped with the work order's user
confirmedRules.parameters: New-row markers: ConcurrencyId = Nothing or "0". Delete threshold: id > 0. Same pattern for instructions (456-482), performed work (484-510), parts (512-538), engineer comments (540-566), mechanic comments (568-594).
edgeCases: The "0" comparison is duplicated in each condition (harmless redundancy)
Upserts run before deletes, so a line both edited and deleted is first updated and then deleted

confirmedRules.name: Work order header fields and status are recorded as supplied; no transition rules in the data layer
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A work order carries a program, aircraft, location, type, status, engineer, engineering action, mechanic, request/fault/due/finish dates and times, three meter readings, aircraft disposition, FIS complaint and squawk numbers, and two alert flags; the data layer stores whatever status is provided without checking allowed transitions.
confirmedRules.given: Work order #1001 in status 'Open' (WorkOrderStatusId 1)
confirmedRules.when: The user saves it with WorkOrderStatusId 3 and a FinishDate
confirmedRules.then: The new status and finish date are written as-is; any rule about which statuses may follow which is enforced elsewhere (UI/business layer or stored procedure), not here
confirmedRules.parameters: Status field: WorkOrderStatusId (status name read back as WorkorderStatus). Alert flags: AircraftIssueAlert, MaintenanceIssueAlert. Soft-delete flag IsDeleted is sent on update but not on insert (new orders start not-deleted). Meters FaultOccurredMeter, MeterStartWork, MeterEndWork sent as decimals.
edgeCases: Dates and times are carried as strings (RequestDate, DueDate, DueTime, FinishDate, FinishTime) and passed to the database unconverted
Field name 'AircraftDispostion' is misspelled consistently in code and database
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: What are the valid work order statuses and allowed transitions (e.g., Open -> In Work -> Closed), and is a finish date/end meter required before closing? None of this is checked in the data access layer.

confirmedRules.name: Meter readings stored as decimals and shown to one decimal place
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Fault-occurred, start-of-work and end-of-work meter readings (e.g. flight hours) are saved as decimals and shown with thousands separators and one decimal place.
confirmedRules.given: A MeterStartWork stored as 1234.56
confirmedRules.then: It is shown as "1,234.6"; on save, the displayed string is converted back with CDec, so 1,234.6 is stored (the second decimal is lost after a load/save round trip)
confirmedRules.parameters: Display format "#,##0.0"; save conversion CDec (lines 201, 206, 209, 324, 329, 332)
edgeCases: Saving an untouched work order can change a stored 2-decimal meter value to 1 decimal
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Round-tripping through the 1-decimal display string silently changes stored meter precision.

confirmedRules.name: Weight definitions stored as whole numbers
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A weight definition (e.g. a standard passenger or cargo weight) belongs to a weight type and a weight unit and is saved as a whole number; fractions are rounded.
confirmedRules.given: A weight definition entered as "185.5" lb
confirmedRules.then: CInt rounds it to 186 (VB banker's rounding: 184.5 would become 184), and it is displayed as "186" using format #,##0
confirmedRules.parameters: Conversion CInt (lines 126, 170); display format "#,##0" (line 229); fields WeightDefTypeId, WeightDefDescr, WeightUnitId, SortOrder, IsActive, IsDeleted
edgeCases: Halves round to even (banker's rounding), not half-up
Insert does not send IsActive/IsDeleted; database defaults apply
List can be filtered by program, weight type id/description, active and deleted flags (lines 57-77)
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Are fractional weights ever legitimate (e.g. kg values), and is round-half-to-even acceptable for weight and balance use?

confirmedRules.name: Daylight-saving begin/end dates are only stored when they are valid dates
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A time zone has a code, UTC offset, description, a daylight-saving on/off flag and a daylight-saving offset; its daylight-saving start and end are saved only if they parse as dates, otherwise they are left empty.
confirmedRules.given: Time zone 'EST' with offset -5, DaylightSavingTime true, DaylightSavingOffset 1, DaylightSavingBegin "03-08-2026 02:00:00 AM" and DaylightSavingEnd "TBD"
confirmedRules.then: Begin is stored as 8 Mar 2026 02:00; End is sent with no value because "TBD" is not a date
confirmedRules.parameters: Offsets stored as float (SQL Float); dates read back formatted "MM-dd-yyyy hh:mm:ss tt" (lines 246-251); same check on insert (lines 183-194)
edgeCases: Null DST dates in the database leave the fields blank on load
No check that Begin is before End or that DST offset is set only when DaylightSavingTime is true
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Invalid dates set the parameter Value to Nothing rather than DBNull.Value; ADO.NET then omits the parameter, which raises a 'procedure expects parameter' error unless the stored procedure declares a default.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is any time conversion (local <-> UTC with DST) actually computed from these fields, and where?

confirmedRules.name: User login returns identity, super-user flag, default program and accessible programs
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A user logs in with user name and password checked by the database; if no match the login fails, otherwise the user gets a display name, last login date, super-user flag, default program and the list of programs they may work in.
confirmedRules.given: User 'jsmith' with a valid password assigned to programs 'Alpha' (ProgId 3, default) and 'Bravo' (ProgId 7)
confirmedRules.then: An authenticated identity is returned with DefaultProgId 3, IsSuperUser as stored, and UserProgramsList = [Alpha, Bravo]; with a wrong password no rows come back and the login returns nothing (rejected)
confirmedRules.parameters: Stored procedure fltValidateLogin(@UserName, @Password); identity created with isLoggedIn = True and program-manager flag initially False (line 116)
edgeCases: Password is passed to the database as given; any hashing/lockout policy lives in the stored procedure
A user with zero programs still logs in, with an empty program list
Any database error becomes a generic error, not a failed login
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Does fltValidateLogin compare hashed passwords and enforce lockout or expiry? The application code sends the raw password.

confirmedRules.name: Per-program manager role and per-module view/edit permissions
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When a user works in a program, the system loads whether they are that program's manager (default No) and, for each application module, whether they can view and whether they can edit.
confirmedRules.given: User 'jsmith' switching to program Bravo (ProgId 7) where the database grants IsProgramManager false and module 'WorkOrders' CanView true, CanEdit false
confirmedRules.then: IsCurrentProgramManager = False and CurrentModulePermissionsList contains (WorkOrders, view yes, edit no), so the user can see but not change work orders
confirmedRules.parameters: Stored procedure fltFetchUserProgramPermissions(@UserName, @ProgId); default IsCurrentProgramManager = False when no row returned
edgeCases: No first result set -> not a program manager
Permissions are appended to the existing list; it is not cleared first, so switching programs repeatedly may accumulate permissions from earlier programs
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: CurrentModulePermissionsList is not cleared before adding (line 91); if the same identity fetches permissions for a second program, it may keep the first program's permissions.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is the permissions list reset elsewhere when the user changes program? If not, a user could keep edit rights from a previous program.

confirmedRules.name: Soft delete with audit stamp for work orders, their lines and master data
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Deleting a work order (or a work-order line, program, route or weight definition) records who deleted it, and these records carry an IsDeleted flag so they are marked deleted rather than removed; region, time zone, weight type and generic lookup deletes carry no user stamp.
confirmedRules.given: Work order #1001 deleted by user 'jsmith'
confirmedRules.then: The record is flagged deleted (IsDeleted=1) with StampUserName 'jsmith' and later appears only in lists that include deleted records
confirmedRules.parameters: Delete with StampUserName: WorkOrder, WorkOrderPart (WorkOrderPartDB.vb:361-377), WO comments/reasons/instructions/performed work, Program (ProgramDB.vb:224-246), Route (RouteDB.vb:197-219), WeightDef (WeightDefDB.vb:197-219). Delete without user: Region (RegionDB.vb:186-207), UTCTimeZone (UTCTimeZoneDB.vb:214-235), WeightDefType, lookup tables (fltLookupBaseDb.vb:187-208).
edgeCases: Whether delete is soft or hard is decided by the stored procedure; inferred from IsDeleted columns and IsDeletedFilter parameters
Every create/update also records StampUserName and database-generated UTC created/modified dates
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Do deleteWorkOrder and the other delete procedures set IsDeleted (soft delete) or physically remove rows, and does deleting a work order cascade to its lines and parts?

confirmedRules.name: Opening a work order loads its lines with the default deleted-record filter
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When a work order is opened, its reasons, instructions, performed work, parts, and engineer and mechanic comments are all loaded with deleted-filter 0 and no paging (all rows).
confirmedRules.given: Work order #1001 has 5 parts, one of them flagged deleted
confirmedRules.then: Parts are listed with IsDeletedFilter 0, Start -1, Count -1 (all pages); whether the deleted part appears depends on what filter value 0 means in listWorkOrderParts
confirmedRules.parameters: IsDeletedFilter = 0, RowStart = -1, RowCount = -1 (lines 35-40)
edgeCases: The standalone GetList wrappers in each child DAL (e.g. WorkOrderPartDB.vb:71, WOEngineerCommentDB.vb:71) ignore the caller's IsDeletedFilter and paging arguments and always pass 0, -1, -1
The TotalRows output is never read back in these child lists
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Child GetList wrappers hard-code 0/-1/-1 and ignore the caller's IsDeletedFilter, RowStart and RowCount.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Does IsDeletedFilter = 0 mean 'exclude deleted' or 'include all'? Should deleted lines ever be shown on a work order?

confirmedRules.name: Linking documents to a work order without duplicates
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When a work order is saved, each attached document's details are updated and a link to the work order is created only if one does not already exist; removing a document from a work order deletes only the link, not the document.
confirmedRules.given: Document 88 already linked to work order #1001 and new document 90 attached
confirmedRules.then: Both documents' info is updated, no second link for 88 is created, a new link 90-1001 is inserted; if document 88 is in the remove list its link is deleted but the document remains
confirmedRules.parameters: DocumentWorkOrderXrefDB.Exists / Insert / Delete stamped with the work order's StampUserName
edgeCases: Document unlinking is processed only on update, not on insert

confirmedRules.name: Work order search filters
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The work order list is always scoped to a program and can be narrowed by aircraft id, free-text aircraft match, location, mechanic, work order number and deleted flag, with paging.
confirmedRules.given: Program 3, aircraft text 'N12', mechanic 14
confirmedRules.then: listWorkOrderInfos returns matching rows with MSN, ship, serial and registration numbers, location, WO number, FIS complaint, squawk, request/due/finish dates and status
confirmedRules.parameters: @ProgId, @AircraftId, @AircraftTextMatch, @LocationId, @MechanicId, @WorkOrderNbr, @IsDeletedFilter, @Start, @Count; @Total output not read back
edgeCases: Matching semantics (exact vs. partial, 0 = any) are defined in the stored procedure
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Which aircraft fields does AircraftTextMatch search (MSN, ship, serial, registration), and does 0 mean 'any' for the id filters?

confirmedRules.name: Program-scoped lookup lists with active flag and sort order
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Generic lookup lists (named code tables) belong to a program and each entry has a text value, sort order and active flag; inactive entries can be filtered out of pick lists.
confirmedRules.given: Lookup 'IssueCode' for program 3 with entry 'Hydraulic leak', sort order 10
confirmedRules.when: An admin adds and later deactivates the entry
confirmedRules.then: addIssueCode creates it (active state from database default), updateIssueCode sets IsActive false so lists filtered by IsActiveFilter can hide it
confirmedRules.parameters: Procedure names built from the lookup name: fetch<Name>, list<Name>s, add<Name>, update<Name>, delete<Name>; filters @ProgId, @IsActiveFilter, paging @Start/@Count
edgeCases: Insert does not send IsActive, so new entries take the database default
Regions (RegionDB.vb) follow the same program-scoped code/name/active pattern
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Are new lookup entries active by default, and can an entry still used by work orders be deleted?

confirmedRules.name: Record version stamp encoded as a decimal string
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The 8-byte database version stamp is turned into a number string by treating each byte as a base-1000 digit, and turned back the same way for the concurrency check on save.
confirmedRules.given: A row version of bytes [0,0,0,0,0,0,7,209]
confirmedRules.when: It is read and later sent back on update
confirmedRules.then: It becomes "7209" (7 x 1000 + 209) and is decoded back to [0,0,0,0,0,0,7,209]
confirmedRules.parameters: Base 1000 per byte, 8 bytes; decode loop covers bytes 1-7 only
edgeCases: Byte 0 is never decoded and is always sent as 0
Values with byte 1 of 10 or more, or any non-zero byte 0, overflow Int64 when encoded
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Encoding overflows Int64 once the database row version passes about 9.2e18 in base-1000 terms (byte 0 non-zero or byte 1 >= 10), and decoding drops byte 0. On a high-volume database this would break every update with false conflicts or errors.

confirmedRules.name: Export file request always asks for changes since 1 January 2000
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When the user clicks Create File, the client asks the server to build an export of all flight-log changes since 01-Jan-2000. The user cannot pick the cut-off date, so every run is effectively a full export.
confirmedRules.given: The client is configured with export credentials
confirmedRules.then: CreateFile is called with ChangesSinceDate = 01-Jan-2000, sent as the form field Date=01-Jan-2000 (format dd-MMM-yyyy, FltExportManager.vb:138). The server's raw response text is added to the activity log.
confirmedRules.parameters: ChangesSinceDate = 01-Jan-2000 (hardcoded); date wire format dd-MMM-yyyy (FltExportManager.vb:138); endpoint key createFileURI = https://flt.contoso.example/export/autoCreateFile.aspx (app.config:24)
edgeCases: The month abbreviation in dd-MMM-yyyy depends on the current culture, so a non-English locale could send a month name the server does not recognize
The CreateFile response is never checked for an <error> element, so a server-side failure shows up only as text in the log
The FltExportManager API takes any date, but the only caller in this module always passes the same fixed date
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is the fixed 01-Jan-2000 cut-off on purpose, so every export is a full export? Or should users choose an incremental 'changes since' date, for example the date of the last successful export?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The date is hardcoded, so incremental export is impossible from the UI. The date is also formatted with the current culture.

confirmedRules.name: Every export service call is authenticated with configured credentials sent in the request
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Each call to the export service (list files, create file, fetch file) sends the user name and password from the app configuration as form fields. The server decides access from these.
confirmedRules.given: app.config holds userName=devuser and password=<credential — masked, see FLTExportClient/app.config:22, preview 'RE**'>
confirmedRules.when: Any of GetFileList, CreateFile or FetchFile runs
confirmedRules.then:
The request body (or the URL query string, if method=GET) is 'UserName=&Password=

[&Date=...|&filename=...]'. The values are joined as raw text with no URL encoding.
confirmedRules.parameters: userName and password app settings (app.config:21-22, loaded in FltExportClient.vb:105-106); method = Post (app.config:19); postData built at FltExportManager.vb:99, 138 and 161
edgeCases: If the method setting is GET, the credentials go into the URL query string (FltExportManager.vb:183-186)
A password containing &, = or + would corrupt the form body, because nothing is URL-encoded
A missing userName or password setting throws a NullReferenceException in the form constructor (.ToString on Nothing)
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The credentials are stored in plain text in app.config and are not URL-encoded. The GET option would expose them in URLs and server logs.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion:
P0 panel split on whether this is critical to the system's core purpose or a costly-if-wrong rule (Faithful: FltExportManager.vb:99 (GetFileList), :138 (CreateFile, adds &Date=dd-MMM-yyyy) and :161 (FetchFile, adds &filename=) build 'UserName=..&Password=..' by plain string concatenation, with no URL encoding. WRequest (:180-201) appends the string to the URL as a query string when the method is GET. When it is POST, it sends the string as an x-www-form-urlencoded body. The method comes from the 'Method' app setting (app.config:19, preview 'Po****'; appSettings lookups ignore case). The credentials are loaded from app.config:21-22 (password preview 'RE****') in FltExportClient.vb:105-106 and passed to all three calls (FltExportClient.vb:22, 47, 75). One small point: the manager also has overloads that take explicit credentials, but the only real caller passes the configured ones, so the rule's 'configured credentials' wording holds. Not P0 under the compliance lens: this is how the client authenticates to a remote API, which is integration plumbing rather than a business rule. The client checks nothing. The server makes the access decision, so no money, regulatory duty or central decision lives in this code. An auditor would care about it, but as a security defect, not as behavior to keep: a plaintext password in config, credentials possibly sent in a GET query string, and no encoding. Making it a P0 behavior contract would force the rewrite to prove it reproduces those defects, when it should replace them with a secrets store and proper encoding. It is better recorded as a security finding or a P1/P2 integration contract (field names UserName/Password/Date/filename, date format dd-MMM-yyyy). I found no instruction-like text in the cited lines. | The rule matches the code. FltExportManager.vb:99, :138 and :161 build postData as "UserName=" & u & "&Password=" & p, then add "&Date=" + Format(date, "dd-MMM-yyyy") for CreateFile or "&filename=" + name for FetchFile. None of the values are URL-encoded. WRequest (:183-186) adds postData to the URL after "?" when the method is GET. For POST (:193-200) it sends postData as an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body. FltExportClient.vb:105-106 loads the credentials from the userName and password app settings, and calls :22, :47 and :75 pass them in. app.config:19 sets Method=Post. The code reads the key "method" in lowercase, but .NET AppSettings lookups ignore case, so the config value is used. The password in app.config:22 is masked here as 'RE****'. The spec leaves out two details: the body is ASCIIEncoding bytes, so non-ASCII characters become '?', and an '&' or '=' in a credential would break the form fields. Neither is enough to make it unfaithful.

P0 is not justified. The client makes no access decision itself. It only sends credentials, and the server decides access, which the rule itself admits. This is integration and transport plumbing (how credentials are sent over HTTP), not a business calculation or decision. It does not move money, enforce regulation, or guard data integrity in this codebase. The real security concern is the plaintext password in app.config:22. That is a finding for the security review, not a P0 behavior to prove equivalent. The exact wire format should be covered by an integration contract test, probably as P1. No instruction-like text was found in the cited lines.) — confirm criticality.

confirmedRules.name: File list response validation and record mapping
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The server's file-list XML is rejected if it contains an <error> element or has no <files> element. Otherwise each <file> becomes a downloadable entry with a name, a size in bytes and a UTC creation time.
confirmedRules.given: The server returns XML such as <files><file><name>flt_20261015.xml</name><size>20480</size><utcDateTimeCreated>2026-10-15T08:00:00</utcDateTimeCreated></file></files>
confirmedRules.then: One entry is listed as flt_20261015.xml, 20,480, 10/15/2026T08:00:00. If the XML has <error>Invalid login</error>, the log shows 'An error occurred:Invalid login'. If there is no <files> element, the log shows 'An error occurred:No files return'.
confirmedRules.parameters: XML tags: error, files, file, name, size, utcDateTimeCreated; size is parsed as a 32-bit integer (CInt)
edgeCases: Child nodes not named 'file' are skipped
A missing name, size or date tag throws an exception and the whole list fails
A file larger than about 2 GB overflows CInt
An empty <files/> element gives an empty list with no error
The list is cleared only after a successful fetch, so on failure the previous list stays on screen
The date display format uses hh (12-hour clock) with no AM/PM marker, so afternoon times are ambiguous (FltExportClient.vb:27)
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The display format 'MM/dd/yyyyThh:mm:ss' uses a 12-hour clock without AM/PM, so 14:00 and 02:00 both show as 02:00.

confirmedRules.name: Exactly one listed file must be selected before fetching
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Only one file can be downloaded at a time, and the user must first select it from the retrieved list. Double-clicking a row does the same as Fetch.
confirmedRules.given: The file list shows several export files and none is selected
confirmedRules.then: The log shows 'No file selected for download' and no request is sent. With one row selected, that row's file name is requested from the fetch endpoint.
confirmedRules.parameters: FileListView.MultiSelect = False (FltExportClient.Designer.vb:66); double-click starts the fetch (FltExportClient.vb:95-99); fetchFileURI = https://flt.contoso.example/export/autoFetchFile.aspx (app.config:25)
edgeCases: Only the first selected item is used
The file name is sent unencoded in the filename form field

confirmedRules.name: Downloaded export is saved to My Documents only when content is non-empty
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A fetched export file is written to the user's My Documents folder under the server-supplied file name, but only if the server returned some content. An existing file with the same name is overwritten.
confirmedRules.given: The user fetched flt_20261015.xml and the server returned 20,480 characters
confirmedRules.then: The content is written to <MyDocuments>\flt_20261015.xml, replacing any existing file, and the log shows 'file written to <path>'. If the content is empty, nothing is written.
confirmedRules.parameters: Destination = Environment.SpecialFolder.MyDocuments; StreamWriter default encoding (UTF-8); overwrites existing files
edgeCases: A non-200 HTTP status gives an empty body, so nothing is written
If the server returns an <error> XML body with HTTP 200, the fetch response is not checked, so the error text is saved as the export file
The file name comes from the server list and is not sanitized, so a name containing ..\ could write outside My Documents
The write happens outside the try block, so an IO failure is not caught by the form's handler
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: FetchFile never checks the response for an <error> element, unlike GetFileList. The server-supplied file name is used in the local path without sanitizing, which allows path traversal.

confirmedRules.name: Export service request policy: configured method, 60-second timeout, HTTP 200 only
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Every export-service call uses the configured HTTP method, follows redirects, and waits at most 60 seconds. Only an HTTP 200 OK response counts as data; any other status is treated as an empty response.
confirmedRules.given: method=Post in configuration
confirmedRules.when: The client calls any export endpoint
confirmedRules.then: It sends an ASCII form-urlencoded POST with a 60,000 ms timeout and returns the body only if the status is 200. Any failure is re-thrown as 'An error occurred: <message>'.
confirmedRules.parameters: Timeout = 60000 ms; UserAgent = http_requestor/0.1; AllowAutoRedirect = True; body encoding ASCII; method key 'Method' = Post (app.config:19, read case-insensitively as 'method')
edgeCases: Non-ASCII characters in the credentials or file name are lost by the ASCII encoding

The dedicated TimeoutException handler in CreateFile (FltExportManager.vb:144-145) and in the form (FltExportClient.vb:52-56) can never run, because WRequest wraps every exception in a generic Exception and HttpWebRequest reports timeouts as WebException
Error messages get nested prefixes, for example 'An error occurred:An error occurred: ...'
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The timeout-specific handling is dead code. A server-side export build that takes longer than 60 seconds shows up as a generic error.

confirmedRules.name: Three-step export workflow: create, list, fetch
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Getting flight-log data out of the system takes three separate steps the user triggers in turn: ask the server to generate an export file, refresh the list of available export files, then download one of them.
confirmedRules.given: No export file has been generated yet
confirmedRules.when: The user clicks Create File, then Get File List, then Fetch File on the new entry
confirmedRules.then: The server generates the file, the file appears in the list with its size and UTC creation time, and the chosen file is saved locally. Each step appends a timestamped line to the activity log ('<now> // <Operation> // <result>').
confirmedRules.parameters: Endpoints: autoCreateFile.aspx, autoGetFileList.aspx, autoFetchFile.aspx (app.config:23-25)
edgeCases: The client does not enforce the order: Fetch only needs a list, and Create does not refresh the list automatically
Whether file creation runs synchronously or in the background on the server cannot be seen from this client
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Does the server build the export file synchronously during the CreateFile call, or in the background? If in the background, how should a user know when the new file is ready to appear in the list?

confirmedRules.name: Export change window: look back a configured number of days
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The scheduled export only includes records changed since 'now minus N days', where N comes from the NbrOfDaysHistory setting (currently 3).
confirmedRules.given: NbrOfDaysHistory = 3 in App.config and the job starts at 2026-10-15 02:00 local time
confirmedRules.when: the export console app computes the ChangesSince date
confirmedRules.then: ChangesSince = 2026-10-12 02:00 local time (Now − 3 days, keeping the time of day), and that value is passed to FltExportManager.CreateDownloadFile, which writes it as the ChangesSince attribute of the export file
confirmedRules.parameters: NbrOfDaysHistory = 3 (App.config:7). The calculation uses local server time from DateTime.Now, not UTC, and keeps the time of day (it is not truncated to midnight).
edgeCases: If the value is not a whole number (e.g. '3.5' or 'abc'), the result of TryParse is ignored and N defaults to 0, so ChangesSince = now and the export is effectively empty, with no warning
If the NbrOfDaysHistory key is missing, .ToString() on Nothing throws, and the run aborts through the general error handler
A negative N gives a future date, so nothing is exported

The function is declared As String, so the date is turned into a string and implicitly parsed back into a Date by CreateDownloadFile. This round trip depends on the culture and drops sub-second precision
The web export page (FLTWebApp/export) uses its own ChangesSinceDate. Its 'all records' overload defaults to 01-Jan-2000
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: An invalid NbrOfDaysHistory silently becomes 0 days because the empty If block after TryParse does nothing. The export then contains no changes and still looks successful. Also, the local-time ChangesSince is formatted by FltExportManager with a 'Z' (UTC) suffix, which may shift the window by the UTC offset.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion:
P0 panel doubts spec fidelity: The basic arithmetic is right: Program.vb:67-69 uses DateTime.Now.AddDays(-nbr), so for N=3 a run at 2026-10-15 02:00 gives 2026-10-12 02:00 local time, with the time of day kept. NbrOfDaysHistory=3 is confirmed at App.config:7. But the card misses or misstates several behaviors that matter if this becomes the equivalence contract.
(1) Silent fallback: the result of Integer.TryParse at Program.vb:63-65 is ignored (the If block is empty). A non-numeric value leaves nbr=0, so ChangesSince = Now and the window is effectively empty. A missing key throws a NullReferenceException at line 59, which is caught at Program.vb:24-28, so no file is produced. The card states neither case.
(2) Text round-trip: GetChangesSinceDate is declared As String (line 57). The DateTime is implicitly converted to a string using the server's regional (culture) settings, then converted back to a Date when CreateDownloadFile(…, ChangesSinceDate As Date, …) is called (FLTBizObjects/BusinessLogic/FltExportManager.vb:28). This drops sub-second precision and depends on the server's regional settings. It is not a clean pass-through.
(3) Wrong UTC label: FltExportManager.vb:16 and :58 write the attribute with the format "yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ". The value is local time, but the attribute shows "2026-10-12T02:00:00Z", which marks it as UTC. The comparison at FltExportManager.vb:297 checks it against UtcDateModified, so local time is compared with UTC.
(4) Scope overstated: the plain-English text says the export "only includes records changed since" the cutoff. The cutoff filter is applied only to flight records (FltExportManager.vb:297). Programs and aircraft are written regardless (lines 60-66, 111).
P0 is justified. The window decides which changes reach the downstream export consumer, so a wrong window silently drops or omits flight changes. It is the central decision of this scheduled export job.
No instruction-shaped text or credential values appear in the cited lines.

confirmedRules.name: Unattended export must run as an authenticated, authorized FLT service user
confirmedRules.source: FLTExportConsoleApp/FLTExportConsoleApp/Program.vb:37-47 (credential target + AuthenticateUserLogin call); FLTBizObjects/BusinessLogic/fltIdentityManager.vb:18-39 (authentication rejections); FLTBizObjects/BusinessLogic/FltExportManager.vb:28-38 (Export CanView authorization); supporting: FLTExportConsoleApp/FLTExportConsoleApp/CredentialHelper.vb:37-60 (credential retrieval only)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Before the export runs, the app reads a username and password from the Windows Credential Manager entry 'FLT.Export.Auth' and logs in to FLT with them. If no credential is stored, login fails, or the user lacks Export view permission, no file is produced.
confirmedRules.given: Windows Credential Manager holds a generic credential with target 'FLT.Export.Auth' for an active, not-deleted, not-locked-out FLT user who has CanView on 'Export'
confirmedRules.then: FltIdentityManager.AuthenticateUserLogin returns an identity, FltExportManager.CanView passes, and the download file is built. If the credential is missing, the run stops with 'Credential not found'. If the account is unknown, deleted or inactive, it stops with 'Failed Login Attempt'. If the account is locked out, it stops with 'User account is locked out'. If the user is not authorized, it stops with 'Can't Export - user is not authorized'
confirmedRules.parameters: Credential target name = 'FLT.Export.Auth' (Program.vb:39). Credential type = CRED_TYPE_GENERIC (1). The password is decoded as a UTF-16 blob of CredentialBlobSize/2 characters. No credential values are stored in source. Authentication is called at Program.vb:43, and the authorization check is in FLTBizObjects/BusinessLogic/FltExportManager.vb:28-38.
edgeCases: If the stored credential has an empty password blob, an empty password is sent to login (and will probably fail)
Lockout policy (Lockout_Duration, MaximumLoginFailuresAllowed) comes from AppConfiguration in FLTBizObjects. Failed logins by the batch job can lock the service account
The identity is resolved while the arguments are evaluated, so the download path and since-date are read first. A config error there aborts the run before authentication
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Citation was corrected by referee (The behavior is real, but the cited lines cover only the first step. CredentialHelper.vb:37-60 reads the stored credential. It calls CredRead with CRED_TYPE_GENERIC (1) and throws 'Credential not found' if that fails (lines 41-42). It decodes the password as UTF-16 with CredentialBlobSize \ 2 characters (line 51). It returns UserName and Password. These lines do no login and no permission check, and those two checks are the core of the rule. The rest of the rule lives elsewhere. Program.vb:39 passes the target 'FLT.Export.Auth' and Program.vb:43 calls FltIdentityManager.AuthenticateUserLogin. Program.vb:22 sends the resulting identity to CreateDownloadFile. FltExportManager.vb:28-38 checks CanView on 'Export' and throws 'Can't Export - user is not authorized' if it fails. fltIdentityManager.vb:18-39 throws 'Failed Login Attempt' when the user is unknown, deleted or inactive, and 'User account is locked out' when the account is locked. All error messages in the rule match the code. Program.vb:24-28 catches every exception, so a failure at any step stops the run and no file is built. No credential values are stored in the source. The cited lines contain no text aimed at an AI or reviewer.) — confirm FLTExportConsoleApp/FLTExportConsoleApp/Program.vb:37-47 (credential target + AuthenticateUserLogin call); FLTBizObjects/BusinessLogic/fltIdentityManager.vb:18-39 (authentication rejections); FLTBizObjects/BusinessLogic/FltExportManager.vb:28-38 (Export CanView authorization); supporting: FLTExportConsoleApp/FLTExportConsoleApp/CredentialHelper.vb:37-60 (credential retrieval only) is the authoritative implementation.

confirmedRules.name: Export run lifecycle: Begin, Export, then End even on failure
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Every run logs 'Begin', tries one export, logs any error, and always logs 'End'. A failed run looks like a normal finish to whatever scheduled it.
confirmedRules.given: the export app is started by a scheduler
confirmedRules.when: any step fails (missing config, missing credential, failed login, not authorized, file write error)
confirmedRules.then: the error message goes to the console and the log (FLTExport.log), 'End FLT Export Console App' is still logged, and the process exits normally with code 0
confirmedRules.parameters: The log is written to a text file only (ContosoLoggerIsWriteTextFile=true; EventLog and DB logging are false; App.config:9-14). Log app name = 'FLTExport'.
edgeCases: A successful run and a failed run both end with the same 'End' banner and exit code
There are no retries. Each scheduled run makes exactly one attempt
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Failures are swallowed and the process returns exit code 0, so the scheduler or monitoring cannot see a failed export.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should a failed export return a non-zero exit code or raise an alert so the downstream consumer knows the daily file is missing?

confirmedRules.name: Export file destination and naming come from configuration
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The export file is written to the folder set in DownloadPath. Its name is meant to include an application prefix and a UTC timestamp, but this app's config does not define the prefix.
confirmedRules.given: DownloadPath is set to a developer workstation folder and no 'appPrefix' key exists in App.config
confirmedRules.then: the file is written as '<DownloadPath>\Download__<yyyyMMddTHHmmssz>.xml' (empty prefix, so two underscores), after first being written as a 'Temp_Download_...' file
confirmedRules.parameters: DownloadPath = developer-machine path under C:\Users\devuser\... (App.config:8). appPrefix is not defined. FltExportManager.vb:47-49 reads it. Read at Program.vb:49-55.
edgeCases: If the DownloadPath key is missing, a NullReferenceException aborts the run
If the folder does not exist or cannot be written, the error is only logged (see the lifecycle rule)
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: What production export folder and appPrefix should the console export use, and does any downstream consumer depend on the file-name prefix?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: App.config has no appPrefix key, so file names have an empty prefix. DownloadPath is hardcoded to a developer's local folder.

confirmedRules.name: Aircraft status code mapping (UP / DOWN / OFF TEST)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Each aircraft is in one of three statuses: stored code 1 means UP, 2 means DOWN, and every other code (including 0 and NULL) means OFF TEST.
confirmedRules.given: An aircraft record with Status = 2
confirmedRules.when: The status is shown on the fleet board or used for filtering
confirmedRules.then: It shows as "DOWN". Status 1 shows as "UP". Status 0, NULL (read as 0) or any unknown value such as 5 shows as "OFF TEST".
confirmedRules.parameters: 1 = UP, 2 = DOWN, anything else = OFF TEST (0 is the explicit code; NULL becomes 0 per AircraftStatusDB.vb:134-138). The edit page writes the dropdown position as the code: position 0 = OFF TEST, 1 = UP, 2 = DOWN (EditAircraftStatus.aspx.vb:20-23, 33, 47).
edgeCases: Unknown codes such as 3 or -1 display as OFF TEST, but EditAircraftStatus sets SelectedIndex = Status, so opening that aircraft for edit throws an out-of-range error
The stored code depends on the order of the dropdown items. Reordering the list silently changes what each code means
There are no transition guards: any status can change to any other status, and the same status can be saved again
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The status code depends on the order of the dropdown items, not on an explicit value, so a code outside 0-2 breaks the edit page.

confirmedRules.name: Main fleet board hides OFF TEST aircraft; OFF TEST view shows the whole fleet
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The default fleet board lists only aircraft that are UP or DOWN. The "Show OFF TEST Fleet" page lists OFF TEST aircraft along with all UP and DOWN aircraft.
confirmedRules.given: A program with aircraft A (UP), B (DOWN) and C (OFF TEST)
confirmedRules.when: A user opens Default.aspx (ShowOffTest=False) or OffTestFleet.aspx (ShowOffTest=True)
confirmedRules.then: Default.aspx shows A and B. OffTestFleet.aspx shows A, B and C.
confirmedRules.parameters: Filter: include when (ShowOffTest AND status='OFF TEST') OR status<>'OFF TEST'. Default.aspx.vb:33 passes False. OffTestFleet.aspx.vb:34 passes True. ProgId is hardcoded to 0 in both pages.
edgeCases: The filter runs in application code after the stored procedure returns every row
On the OFF TEST page, the button that goes back is labelled "Show ON TEST Fleet" (OffTestFleet.aspx:22)
ProgId 0 is always sent to listAircraftStatuses. What 0 means (all programs?) is set inside the stored procedure
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should the OFF TEST page list only OFF TEST aircraft? Today it shows the whole fleet. Also, what does ProgId = 0 select in listAircraftStatuses?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The page name and button suggest an OFF TEST-only view, but the OR condition also includes every UP and DOWN aircraft.

confirmedRules.name: Fleet visibility requires Fleet CanView permission
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A user sees the fleet list only if they hold View rights on the "Fleet" resource. Otherwise the list comes back empty.
confirmedRules.given: A logged-in user without the Fleet CanView right
confirmedRules.then: GetList returns Nothing, and the grid shows "No Records Retrieved" with no error message
confirmedRules.parameters: Resource name "Fleet", action fltUserAction.CanView (resolved by FltIdentityManager.AuthorizeUserAction in FLTBizObjects)
edgeCases: The user cannot tell a permission denial apart from an empty fleet
EditAircraftStatus.aspx loads and shows any aircraft by ID from the query string without checking CanView
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The edit page reads aircraft details by ID (query string v) without a CanView check.

confirmedRules.name: Aircraft status editing requires Fleet CanEdit plus a role time window
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A user can change an aircraft's status only with Fleet Edit rights and only during an edit time window set for one of their roles. Super users can edit at any time.
confirmedRules.given: A non-super user who holds Fleet CanEdit and is in role 3 (window 08:00-14:30 PT)
confirmedRules.when: They open an aircraft at 14:31 PT
confirmedRules.then: Editing is refused: the page shows "You cannot edit the aircraft status at this time." and disables Save, Status and both comment fields. At 14:30 PT, editing is allowed.
confirmedRules.parameters: Time is coded as HHMM (hour*100+minute), and both window ends are inclusive. Role 3: 08:00-14:30. Role 7: 08:00-16:00 (Web.config:10-17). Super users bypass the window. Fleet CanEdit is checked first.
edgeCases: A user with several roles is allowed if any one role's window matches
A role with no window configured (any of the 4 keys missing) never allows editing, unless the user is a super user
Windows cannot cross midnight because the comparison is simple
Day of week and holidays are ignored
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: SaveButton_Click (EditAircraftStatus.aspx.vb:46-49) saves without checking CanEdit again on the server. Only the page controls are disabled, so a crafted postback, or a page loaded before the window closed, can still save after hours or without rights.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion:
P0 panel doubts spec fidelity: P0 is justified. This is the authorization gate on who can change an aircraft's UP/DOWN/OFF TEST status and when. That is security and data-integrity control over operational fleet state, not a minor validation.

Fidelity is only partial. Several parts match the code. AircraftStatusManager.vb:28-29 checks Fleet CanEdit first. Lines 37-39 let super users bypass the window. Line 42 codes the time as Hour*100+Minute. Lines 50-51 make both window ends inclusive, using >= and <=. Lines 45-55 allow editing if any of the user's roles has an open window. The windows in FltFleet/Web.config:10-17 are role 3 = 08:00-14:30 and role 7 = 08:00-16:00. The message and the four disabled controls match FltFleet/EditAircraftStatus.aspx.vb:34-40. Under a Pacific-zone server, the boundary cases (14:30 allowed, 14:31 refused) are correct.

The card is wrong or incomplete on three points that matter for a behavior contract:

1. **"PT" is not what the code computes.** GetCurrentTimeInPT (lines 85-97) works from the server's StandardName. Eastern subtracts 3 hours and Mountain subtracts 1. Central sets 2 at line 91, but line 93 checks "central" again and overwrites it with 0, so a Central server applies no offset and treats Central time as PT. Any zone not matched, including Pacific, also gets 0. A fixed hour offset also ignores DST differences. So "14:31 PT" only holds on a Pacific or Mountain server, and only if DST lines up. On a Central server, 14:31 Central is treated as 14:31 PT, two hours off.
2. **"Editing is refused" is only enforced in the page display.** The check runs only on the initial page load (the else-free branch inside the non-postback block). SaveButton_Click (EditAircraftStatus.aspx.vb:45-48) calls AircraftStatusDB.SaveStatusUpdate without checking CanEdit again. Refusal therefore depends on disabled controls in the browser. A forged postback, or a page opened before the window closed and saved after it, still saves.
3. **Missing edge case.** A non-super user with CanEdit whose roles have no ChangeTime* keys (any role other than 3 or 7) is always refused. GetEditTimeRangeForRole returns False when a key is empty (lines 65-79), so CanEdit alone never grants editing without a configured window.

No instruction-shaped text was found in the cited lines and no credentials were present.

confirmedRules.name: Role edit time windows are configuration-driven
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Each role's allowed editing hours come from four settings per role: start hour, start minute, stop hour and stop minute. If any one is missing, that role has no edit window.
confirmedRules.given: Web.config sets ChangeTimeStartHourFor7=8, StartMinute=0, StopHour=16, StopMinute=0
confirmedRules.when: Edit permission is checked for a role 7 user
confirmedRules.then: Role 7 may edit from 08:00 to 16:00 PT inclusive
confirmedRules.parameters: Keys: ChangeTimeStartHourFor{RoleId}, ChangeTimeStartMinuteFor{RoleId}, ChangeTimeStopHourFor{RoleId}, ChangeTimeStopMinuteFor{RoleId}. Configured values: role 3 = 8:00-14:30, role 7 = 8:00-16:00 (FltFleet/Web.config:10-17).
edgeCases: A missing key yields an empty value, so the role is treated as having no window
A non-numeric value throws a conversion error and the edit check fails with an exception

confirmedRules.name: Current Pacific Time derivation for edit window
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The system estimates the current Pacific time by taking the server's local time and subtracting hours based on the server's time-zone name.
confirmedRules.given: A server whose standard time-zone name contains "Eastern", at 17:00 local time
confirmedRules.then: Pacific time is computed as 14:00 (17:00 - 3h)
confirmedRules.parameters: Eastern = -3h, Mountain = -1h, Central = -2h but then overwritten to 0 (line 93). Any other zone = 0h.
edgeCases: A server in Central time gets 0 hours subtracted, so the edit window is judged 2 hours late
A server in Pacific or UTC gets 0 hours subtracted. A UTC server would be 7-8 hours off
Matching uses a substring of the lowercase StandardName
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Line 93 checks "central" a second time and sets the offset to 0. The developer almost certainly meant "pacific". As a result, Central-zone servers apply no correction.

confirmedRules.name: Last-update timestamp displayed in Pacific Time
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Each aircraft's last-modified UTC time is shown as Pacific Time by subtracting 8 hours, or 9 hours when the server is currently on daylight saving time.
confirmedRules.given: UTCDateModified = 2026-07-01 20:00 UTC and the server is on DST today
confirmedRules.when: The fleet board shows the "Last Update (PT)" column
confirmedRules.then: It displays 2026-07-01 11:00 (20:00 - 9h). The real PDT time is 13:00.
confirmedRules.parameters: Standard offset -8h. DST offset -9h. DST is judged from the server's local zone on today's date (Date.Now), not on the record's date.
edgeCases: UTCDateModified of MinValue or NULL displays blank
Any exception displays blank
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Pacific Daylight Time is UTC-7, not UTC-9, so DST timestamps are 2 hours early. DST is also taken from the current date on the server, not from the record's date.

confirmedRules.name: Aircraft status update and its comments
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: An authorized user changes an aircraft's status and its two free-text comments (hangar/engineer and Contoso) in one save, and the record's modified time is updated.
confirmedRules.given: Aircraft 42 is DOWN with Hangar comment "Hydraulic leak"
confirmedRules.when: An authorized user selects UP, enters a comment and clicks Save
confirmedRules.then: updateAircraftStatus is called with AircraftId=42, Status=1 and both comments (HTML-decoded), and the user returns to the fleet board. Cancel returns without saving.
confirmedRules.parameters: Comment max length is 100 characters, set only by the textbox MaxLength (EditAircraftStatus.aspx:27,31). The stored procedure updateAircraftStatus is expected to set UTCDateModified (not visible in this module).
edgeCases: UI labels are swapped compared with field names: EngineerComment is labelled "Hangar Comment(s)" and HangarComment is labelled "Contoso Comment(s)"
The 100-character limit is enforced only in the browser
There is no audit of who made the change at this layer
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Does updateAircraftStatus record who made the change and set UTCDateModified, or keep a status history? Should comments be limited to 100 characters on the server as well?

confirmedRules.name: Login required for all fleet pages; session lifetime
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Every fleet page sends the user to the login page unless the session holds a logged-in identity. Sessions and form logins expire after 30 minutes of inactivity.
confirmedRules.given: A user whose session has been idle for 31 minutes
confirmedRules.when: They request Default.aspx, OffTestFleet.aspx or EditAircraftStatus.aspx
confirmedRules.then: They are redirected to Login.aspx
confirmedRules.parameters: Session timeout 30 min, forms timeout 30 min (Web.config:52-55). Same guard in OffTestFleet.aspx.vb:14-17 and EditAircraftStatus.aspx.vb:13-16.
edgeCases: Logout clears and abandons the session, expires the session cookie, and redirects to Login (Logout.aspx.vb:8-17)

confirmedRules.name: Login failure and password recovery do not reveal which accounts exist
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Failed logins always show the same generic message, and password recovery always shows the 'new password sent' confirmation whether or not the username exists.
confirmedRules.given: A visitor enters an unknown username on the password recovery page
confirmedRules.then: No password is generated, but the confirmation view ("A new password has been generated...") is still shown
confirmedRules.parameters: Login failure text: "Failed Login Attempt - either Username or Password is incorrect" (Login.aspx.vb:18-34). Password generation and email are done in FltUserManager.GenerateNewPassword.
edgeCases: For a known user, anyone who knows the username can trigger a password reset with no further verification
Login.aspx.vb declares a _loginTrys counter but never uses it, so this module has no lockout
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is it intended that anyone who knows a username can reset that user's password without verification, and that this module enforces no login lockout or attempt limit?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: An unauthenticated caller can force a password reset for any known username, which makes denial of service by resets possible.

confirmedRules.name: Client and authorization errors are shown as a generic 'Page Not Found' page
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When a request fails because it was bad, unauthenticated, payment-required, forbidden or not found, the user is redirected to a single 'Page Not Found' page, so nothing reveals whether the resource exists or that access was refused.
confirmedRules.given: A user of the Aircraft Status Monitor requests a page they are not allowed to see (HTTP 403), or a URL that does not exist (HTTP 404)
confirmedRules.then: The browser is redirected (HTTP 302) to /ErrorPages/NotFound.aspx, which shows 'Page Not Found - The page you requested could not be found.' The page does no further processing: Page_Load is empty (NotFound.aspx.vb:6-8)
confirmedRules.parameters: Status codes mapped: 400, 401, 402, 403, 404; subStatusCode=-1 (all); responseMode=Redirect; target path /ErrorPages/NotFound.aspx (wiring is in FltFleet/Web.config:71-82)
edgeCases: 401 and 403 (authentication and authorization failures) are deliberately disguised as 'not found'
responseMode=Redirect means the final response the client sees is a 200 for NotFound.aspx, not the original status code
5xx server errors are not mapped here
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is it deliberate security policy to show 401/403 (access denied) as 'Page Not Found', and must the rewrite keep this? Also, should the original status code be kept instead of a redirect that returns 200?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Because the response is a redirect, the client and monitoring tools see a successful 200 page instead of the original 4xx status code. A 401 that redirects to an anonymous page also skips any login challenge.

confirmedRules.name: Unhandled-error page says the administrator was notified, but nothing sends a notification
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The generic error page tells users 'The website administrator has been notified', but no code that sends that notification was found, and no configuration in the files checked sends users to this page.
confirmedRules.given: An unhandled server error happens while a user is working in FLTFleet
confirmedRules.then: The page shows 'An Error Has Occurred - There was a problem encountered with your last request. The website administrator has been notified.' Its code-behind Page_Load is empty (Oops.aspx.vb:6-8), so the page itself sends no notification and logs nothing
confirmedRules.parameters: Message text only; no notification channel, recipient or threshold appears in the code
edgeCases: No reference to Oops.aspx was found in Web.config httpErrors (only 4xx codes are mapped, all to NotFound.aspx), and no Application_Error, mail or SMTP handler was found by grep in Global.asax.vb
Any notification would have to happen somewhere else (for example a logging module); none was found in these files
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: How is the administrator actually notified of unhandled errors (ELMAH, Application_Error, an email or monitoring tool), and how do users reach Oops.aspx? Should the rewrite actually send this notification?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The promise to users ('administrator has been notified') appears only in the page text. No code that sends a notification and no routing to this page was found.

confirmedRules.name: Only logged-in users may view application pages
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Any page that uses the main layout, plus the home page, sends the visitor to the Login page unless the session holds a user identity marked as logged in.
confirmedRules.given: A visitor whose session identity is the anonymous identity created when the session started (IsLoggedIn = False)
confirmedRules.when: They request /Default.aspx or any page built on FLT.Master (including the NotFound and Oops error pages)
confirmedRules.then: They are redirected to ~/Login.aspx. Otherwise the page shows the user's display name and last login date in the footer and builds the program list and menu on first load.
confirmedRules.parameters: Session key 'fltIdentity'; redirect target ~/Login.aspx. The same check is repeated in FLTWebApp/Default.aspx.vb:11-18.
edgeCases: Session_Start (Global.asax.vb:23-26) always places a new, not-logged-in FltIdentity in session, so the identity is normally present but anonymous
The error pages ErrorPages/NotFound.aspx and ErrorPages/Oops.aspx use FLT.Master, so an anonymous user who hits an error is sent to Login and never sees the error page
The identity is written back to session on PreRender (FLT.Master.vb:32-34)
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The guard uses VB 'Or' instead of 'OrElse' (FLT.Master.vb:19, Default.aspx.vb:14). If the session identity is ever Nothing, evaluating fltIdentity.IsLoggedIn throws a NullReferenceException instead of redirecting.

confirmedRules.name: Login authentication with a single generic failure message
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A user logs in with username and password. On success their identity is stored in the session and they go to the home page. Any failure shows the same message so the user cannot tell which part was wrong.
confirmedRules.given: User 'jdoe' enters a wrong password, or is unknown, deleted, inactive or locked out
confirmedRules.then: The page shows 'Failed Login Attempt - either Username or Password is incorrect'. With valid credentials the session identity is replaced with the authenticated identity, which carries program permissions, and the user is redirected to ~/default.aspx.
confirmedRules.parameters: The business checks in FltIdentityManager.AuthenticateUserLogin (FLTBizObjects/BusinessLogic/fltIdentityManager.vb:18-76) run in this order: user exists, not deleted, active, not locked out, password hash matches. 'Remember me' is turned off (Login.aspx:20). Password field autocomplete is off (Login.aspx.vb:14).

confirmedRules.name: Account lockout after repeated failed logins
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: After 5 wrong passwords in a row an account is locked for 10 minutes. The first login attempt after the 10 minutes clears the lock and the failure count.

confirmedRules.when: jdoe enters a wrong password a fifth time at 09:00 UTC
confirmedRules.then: The account is marked IsLockedOut = True with the window start set to 09:00 UTC. Every attempt before 09:10 UTC is rejected even if the password is correct. An attempt at or after 09:10 UTC unlocks the account and resets the count to 0, then checks the password again.
confirmedRules.parameters: LockoutDuration = 10 (minutes; falls back to 5 if not numeric, AppConfig.vb:32-44); MaximumLoginFailuresAllowed = 5 (falls back to 3 if not numeric, AppConfig.vb:46-58). Logic is in fltIdentityManager.vb:37-62: if count < (max - 1) the count is incremented, otherwise the account is locked.
edgeCases: The lock happens on the Nth failure (count reaches max-1 and the next failure locks), so 5 failures lock the account
Lock expiry uses DateDiff in whole minutes, measured from UtcFailedPasswordAttemptWindowStart (the moment of lockout)
Failures are not windowed by time; the count builds up until a successful login or an unlock
The appSetting 'BatchLoginMode' = 'Both' is defined at Web.config:65 but is not referenced in this module
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The count is not time-windowed even though the field is named 'FailedPasswordAttemptWindowStart', so old failures from days ago still count toward lockout.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion:
Citation was corrected by referee (The behavior is real, but the cited lines don't implement it. FLTWebApp/Web.config:79-80 only holds the two settings, LockoutDuration=10 and MaximumLoginFailuresAllowed=5. The lockout logic itself is in FLTBizObjects/BusinessLogic/fltIdentityManager.vb:37-62. The rule matches that code:
- Line 37: a locked account is rejected while DateDiff(Minute, UtcFailedPasswordAttemptWindowStart, UtcNow) < Lockout_Duration. The password is never checked in that case.
- Lines 41-45: otherwise, a locked account is unlocked, its count is reset to 0, it is saved and reloaded, and the password check runs next (lines 49-50).
- Line 51: on a wrong password, if count < (Max - 1), the count goes up by 1 (lines 52-55).
- Lines 57-61: otherwise IsLockedOut is set to True and the window start is set to UtcNow.
With count=4 and max=5, 4 < 4 is false, so the fifth failure locks the account, as the rule says.
The fallbacks are confirmed in FLTBizObjects/DataAccess/AppConfig.vb: LockoutDuration falls back to 5 at lines 32-44 and MaximumLoginFailuresAllowed falls back to 3 at lines 46-58.
Small detail: VB DateDiff with DateInterval.Minute counts minute boundaries crossed, not minutes actually elapsed. So the real lock can be up to about 1 minute shorter than 10 minutes when the lock starts partway through a minute. The rule's example uses exact on-the-minute times, so it is still correct.
On a successful login, lines 68-70 also reset IsLockedOut and the count.
The cited lines contain no instruction-shaped text.) — confirm FLTBizObjects/BusinessLogic/fltIdentityManager.vb:37-62 (parameters: FLTWebApp/Web.config:79-80, FLTBizObjects/DataAccess/AppConfig.vb:32-58) is the authoritative implementation.

confirmedRules.name: Authenticated session required for configuration and document pages
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Only a logged-in user can open the document or reference-data pages. Anyone else is sent away before any data is read or changed.
confirmedRules.given: A request arrives with no FltIdentity in the session, or with an identity whose IsLoggedIn = False
confirmedRules.when: Any of the DocumentTypes, TimeZones, WeightDefTypes, programs, DocumentAdd, documentsList or DocumentShow pages loads
confirmedRules.then: The user is redirected to ~/Login.aspx. DocumentShow sends them to ~/NotAuthorized.aspx instead, so no document is streamed.

confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Because 'Or' does not short-circuit, a missing session crashes the page instead of redirecting. Use OrElse.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion:
P0 panel doubts spec fidelity: P0 is justified. This is the authentication gate in front of document download and changes to reference data, so it guards security and data integrity. The Given/When/Then is wrong on one of its two branches, though.

1. **The "no FltIdentity in session" branch.** The gate at FLTWebApp/documents/DocumentShow.aspx.vb:17 (and the same line on every other cited page) uses VB.NET `Or`, not `OrElse`. `Or` evaluates both sides. When Session("fltIdentity") is Nothing, `_fltIdentity.IsLoggedIn` is still evaluated and throws a NullReferenceException. So the request fails with an unhandled error. It is not redirected to ~/Login.aspx or ~/NotAuthorized.aspx, which is what the rule claims. This case can happen: Global.asax.vb:23-26 seeds a new FLTIdentity at Session_Start, but FLTWebApp/export/autoUtilityProcs.vb:20 sets Session("fltIdentity") = Nothing, and Logout.aspx.vb:11-12 clears the session. Access is still blocked, because the exception stops the page before any data is read. But the behavior a modernized system must match is "error", not "redirect".

2. **The IsLoggedIn = False branch matches the code.** FltIdentity._isLoggedIn defaults to False (FLTBizObjects/BusinessObject/fltIdentity.vb:11). The one-argument Response.Redirect ends the request before DownloadDocument or any data binding runs. DocumentShow goes to ~/NotAuthorized.aspx and the other six pages go to ~/Login.aspx, as stated. All six parallel citations check out.

3. **Minor point.** documentsList.aspx.vb calls ClearErrorFields() before the gate (line 21). This only touches the UI, so "sent away before any data is read or changed" still holds.

4. **Correction needed.** Split the Given into two cases. (a) Identity present with IsLoggedIn = False: redirect. (b) Identity missing (Nothing): a NullReferenceException is thrown and the page fails before any data access. Also flag the `Or` vs `OrElse` defect for an SME to decide whether the modernized system should keep it.

No instruction-shaped text or credentials were found in the cited lines.
