confirmedRules.name: Export access requires the Export/CanView permission (session reuse or batch re-login)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Only a logged-in user whose role grants the 'Export' View permission may create, list or download flight-data export files. Batch callers reuse their session identity or are re-authenticated from the request credentials on every call.
confirmedRules.given: A batch client calls autoCreateFile, autoGetFileList or autoFetchFile, or a user opens export.aspx
confirmedRules.when: The session has no identity or the identity is not logged in
confirmedRules.then: Batch pages try AuthenticateUser from the request credentials. If the resulting identity fails FltExportManager.CanView (AuthorizeUserAction(identity, "Export", CanView)), the response is <error>User is not authorized</error>. The interactive page sends the user to ~/Login.aspx. An authorized user goes on to the requested export action.
confirmedRules.and: FltExportManager.CreateDownloadFile checks CanView again and throws 'Can't Export - user is not authorized' if it fails (FLTBizObjects/BusinessLogic/FltExportManager.vb:28-38)
confirmedRules.parameters: Permission object = "Export"; action = fltUserAction.CanView; session key = "fltIdentity"
edgeCases: The same guard appears in autoFetchFile.aspx.vb:17-26, autoGetFileList.aspx.vb:15-23 and export.aspx.vb:14-17
export.aspx.vb:27 saves the identity under the session key "_fltIdentity", but every reader uses "fltIdentity", so that write has no effect

export.aspx.vb:137 builds download links straight to ~/download/<file>. No <location> rule protecting /download was found in FLTWebApp/Web.config, so anyone who knows a file name may be able to fetch an export without the CanView check
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The guard uses non-short-circuit `Or`: `(_fltIdentity Is Nothing) Or (_fltIdentity.IsLoggedIn = False)`. When the identity is Nothing, the second operand still runs and throws NullReferenceException, so first-time batch calls with no session may crash instead of authenticating. The /download folder also appears to be served as static content, which skips authorization.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: P0 panel doubts spec fidelity: P0 is justified. This is the access-control gate on bulk flight-data export, so it guards security and data confidentiality. The rule's core is right: autoCreateFile.aspx.vb:24-25 and the matching checks in autoGetFileList.aspx.vb:22 and autoFetchFile.aspx.vb:25 call FltExportManager.CanView, which is AuthorizeUserAction(identity, "Export", CanView) (FltExportManager.vb:36-38). CreateDownloadFile checks again and throws 'Can't Export - user is not authorized' (FltExportManager.vb:28-34). But the Given/When/Then gets four edge cases wrong. (1) The 'no identity' case fails differently than stated. Lines 18 (autoCreateFile), 17 (autoGetFileList), 19 (autoFetchFile) and export.aspx.vb:15 use VB 'Or', which does not short-circuit. When Session("fltIdentity") is Nothing, the code still evaluates _fltIdentity.IsLoggedIn and throws a NullReferenceException. So a session with no identity never reaches AuthenticateUser, and export.aspx never redirects to ~/Login.aspx. Only a session that holds an identity with IsLoggedIn = False takes the re-login or redirect path. (2) The 'User is not authorized' response is not what a failed re-login returns. When AuthenticateUser fails (missing username/password, bad login, or an exception), InvalidLogin writes '<error>Invalid Login</error>' and ends the response (autoUtilityProcs.vb:44-58, 84-93). The CanView check never runs, so <error>User is not authorized</error> appears only for a logged-in identity that lacks the permission. (3) If the identity ever reached CanView as Nothing, AuthorizeUserAction would throw 'FltIdentity is nothing' (fltIdentityManager.vb:98-99), not return false. (4) The rule leaves out the bypasses in AuthorizeUserAction (fltIdentityManager.vb:102-105): a super user, or a current program manager (for any module except security and appconfig), gets Export view access without holding an explicit 'Export' module permission. Two smaller points: the credential source depends on BatchLoginMode (get, post or both), and in 'both' mode the query-string key is 'userName' (autoUtilityProcs.vb:34). No credential values or injection-shaped text appear in the cited lines.

confirmedRules.name: Batch login credential source is set by BatchLoginMode
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Automated export clients must send a username and password. The BatchLoginMode setting decides whether they are read from the URL query string, the posted form, or both (query string first).
confirmedRules.given: BatchLoginMode = "Both" (current Web.config value) and a request with ?username=svc_export&password=****
confirmedRules.when: An automated export page needs to authenticate the caller
confirmedRules.then: The credentials come from the query string (the form is used only if the query-string username is empty). Missing username or password returns <error>Invalid Login</error> and logs 'Missing username/password'. A rejected login or an exception also returns Invalid Login. A successful login stores the identity in Session("fltIdentity").
confirmedRules.parameters: BatchLoginMode values: get | post | both (Web.config value "Both", lower-cased); field names username, password; credential values: <credential — supplied at runtime, never hardcoded>
edgeCases: Mode 'get' reads only the query string, 'post' only the form

The fallback branch is `Case "else"` (a literal string), not `Case Else`. An unrecognised mode is not reported as a configuration error. Credentials stay empty and the caller gets 'Missing username/password'
The failed-login log message includes the attempted username
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: `Case "else"` should be `Case Else`, so a misconfigured BatchLoginMode is never reported. 'get' and 'both' modes accept passwords in the URL query string, where they can end up in web server and proxy logs.

confirmedRules.name: Automated export creation requires a valid changes-since date
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A batch request to build an export file must supply a 'date' parameter that parses as a date. Only then is an export of data changed since that date built.
confirmedRules.given: An authorized batch caller and BatchLoginMode = both
confirmedRules.then: FltExportManager.CreateDownloadFile builds an export containing flights modified on or after 2026-10-01 00:00
confirmedRules.and: If the date is missing or empty, the reply is <error>Date is missing/invalid</error>. If it is not a parseable date (e.g. 'yesterday'), the reply is <error>Date is Invalid</error>. No file is created in either case.
confirmedRules.parameters: Request field "date"; script timeout 300 seconds; the source (query string vs form) follows BatchLoginMode, falling back to the form in 'both' mode when the query-string value is empty
edgeCases: The date is parsed with the server culture (IsDate/implicit DateTime conversion), so 01/02/2026 may mean Jan 2 or Feb 1
There is no lower or upper bound: a future date gives an export with no flights, and a very old date gives a full export

confirmedRules.name: Interactive export cutoff: default yesterday or full history
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: On the Export page the user picks either 'only flight data recorded on or after a date' (defaults to yesterday) or 'include all flight data'. The second option uses 1 January 1900 as the cutoff.
confirmedRules.given: Today is 10/15/2026 and the page is first loaded
confirmedRules.when: The user clicks Create Export File
confirmedRules.then: With the first option the cutoff is the entered date (pre-filled with 10/14/2026, i.e. today minus 1 day, MM/dd/yyyy). With 'Include All Flight Data' the cutoff is 01/01/1900. The export includes only flights whose UTC modified date is on or after the cutoff (FltExportManager.vb:297).
confirmedRules.and: If the first option is selected and the text is not a valid date, the error 'Flights Since Date is a required date value.' is shown and no file is created
confirmedRules.parameters: Default lookback = 1 day (Date.Now.AddDays(-1)); full-history sentinel = 01/01/1900; the business-layer overload without a date uses 01-Jan-2000 (FltExportManager.vb:22)
edgeCases: Switching to 'Include All' disables the date box and shows 'Not Applicable' (export.aspx.vb:30-39)
The cutoff applies only to flights (Usages). Programs, aircraft, configurations and locations are always exported in full
The cutoff is a local-time date but is compared to the flight's UtcDateModified
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: There are two different 'all data' sentinels (1900-01-01 on the page, 2000-01-01 in the business-layer overload), so the overload silently leaves out pre-2000 changes. The local-date cutoff is compared with UTC modification timestamps.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should the 'all data' cutoff be the same everywhere (1900 vs 2000)? Should the changes-since date be read as local time or UTC?

confirmedRules.name: Export files are kept for 24 hours, purged when the file list is viewed
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Generated export files are deleted from the download folder once they are more than 24 hours old. The purge runs only when someone lists the available files.
confirmedRules.given: The download folder has Download_X_20261014T080000.xml created 2026-10-14 08:00 UTC and another file created 2026-10-15 07:00 UTC
confirmedRules.when: At 2026-10-15 09:00 UTC a batch client calls autoGetFileList or a user opens or refreshes the Export page
confirmedRules.then: The first file (created + 24h = 10-15 08:00, earlier than now) is deleted. The second is kept and listed with its name, size in bytes and UTC creation time.
confirmedRules.parameters: Retention ageInHours = 24 (hardcoded twice: autoGetFileList.aspx.vb:88 and export.aspx.vb:90); based on file CreationTimeUtc; top-level folder ~/download only
edgeCases: The same logic is duplicated in export.aspx.vb:89-98 (ShowXmlFiles)
Creating a file (autoCreateFile) or fetching one (autoFetchFile) does not purge, so an expired file can still be downloaded until someone lists the folder
The list includes every file in the folder, including in-progress 'Temp_Download_*' files and non-export files
On the Export page an empty folder shows 'There are currently no XML Export files available for download.'
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Retention is enforced only as a side effect of listing, so files can stay past 24 hours and still be fetched by name.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is 24 hours the required retention for export files? Should purging be scheduled rather than triggered by viewing the list?

confirmedRules.name: Fetch an export file only when the name matches exactly one file
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: An automated client downloads an export by naming it. The file is sent as XML only if the name matches exactly one file in the download folder.
confirmedRules.given: An authorized caller and a download folder containing Download_FLT_20261015T090000+0.xml
confirmedRules.then: The file is streamed as text/xml with its Content-Length
confirmedRules.and: A missing or empty filename gives <error>No file requested</error>. Zero matches or more than one match gives <error>File not found</error>.
confirmedRules.parameters: Request field "filename"; search scope = ~/download top directory only; FileBufferSize = 4096 bytes (Web.config)
edgeCases: The filename is used as a DirectoryInfo.GetFiles search pattern, so wildcards work: 'D*.xml' downloads a file whenever only one file matches
An in-progress Temp_Download_* file can be fetched if named
Files older than 24 hours can still be fetched if no listing has purged them yet
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: SendFile writes a full bufferSize (4096 bytes) on every loop instead of the number of bytes read, so the last chunk adds stale or zero bytes after the real data. The output is then longer than the declared Content-Length and the XML may be corrupted. Using the caller's filename as a search pattern allows wildcard matching.

confirmedRules.name: Export file is built under a temporary name, then published with a UTC-timestamped name
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Each export run writes a temporary file. When the file is complete it is renamed to a final name built from the app prefix and the UTC creation timestamp, and only then does it become the published download.
confirmedRules.given: appPrefix = FLT and an export started at 2026-10-15 09:00:00 UTC
confirmedRules.when: CreateDownloadFile runs (from autoCreateFile or the Export page button)
confirmedRules.then: It writes Temp_Download_FLT_20261015T090000<offset>.xml, then renames it to Download_FLT_20261015T090000<offset>.xml in ~/download
confirmedRules.and: Whenever a file is written, Programs > Fleet > Aircraft > Locations > Flights are included. For aircraft with flights at locations they have no AircraftLocation record for, the export inserts a new AircraftLocation record (ArrivalDate = now UTC, StampUserName = 'export'), as a side effect in the database (FltExportManager.vb:187-199)
confirmedRules.parameters: Name pattern Download_<appPrefix>_<yyyyMMddTHHmmssz>.xml (FltExportManager.vb:46-49); download dir ~/download (autoUtilityProcs.vb:12)
edgeCases: Two exports in the same second get the same name, and the rename fails
If generation fails, the Temp_ file is left behind and shows in listings until purged
The 'z' format specifier writes the server's local UTC offset, even though the timestamp itself is UTC
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Running an export, which looks like a read-only operation, writes AircraftLocation rows to the database. Timestamp names with one-second resolution can collide.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is it intended that generating an export creates missing AircraftLocation records (stamped 'export')? Should the file timestamp suffix show the server's local offset when the time is UTC?

confirmedRules.name: Flight total hours and ending airframe hours from Hobbs meter
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A flight's total hours are the Hobbs end reading minus the Hobbs start reading, and the aircraft's ending airframe hours are the Hobbs end reading plus the meter offset in effect for that flight.
confirmedRules.given: A flight with Hobbs start 1,234.5, Hobbs end 1,236.0 and a used meter offset of 500.0
confirmedRules.when: The user changes either the Hobbs start or Hobbs end field
confirmedRules.then: Total hours shows 1.5 (1,236.0 - 1,234.5) and airframe hours end shows 1,736.0 (1,236.0 + 500.0), both formatted to one decimal place; both Hobbs fields are reformatted to one decimal
confirmedRules.and: In edit mode the stored flight shows total hours as AirframeHoursEnd - AirframeHoursStart (line 417)
confirmedRules.parameters: Meter display mask '#,##0.0;-#,##0.0' (one decimal, negatives allowed) at FlightModify.aspx.vb:20
edgeCases: Recalculation only happens when both Hobbs values are numeric; otherwise the previous totals stay displayed
No check that Hobbs end >= Hobbs start in the page; a negative total is displayed with the negative mask
Calculated airframe hours end is read back from a label and saved to the flight in LoadDataToObject (line 495)
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The page does not reject Hobbs end lower than Hobbs start; any such check must live in FlightManager.Save business rules (not verified here).

confirmedRules.name: New flight starting meter values default from aircraft's current readings

confirmedRules.when: A user starts adding a new flight for that aircraft
confirmedRules.then: Airframe hours start shows 1,736.0, used meter offset 500.0, Hobbs start 1,236.0 (1,736.0 - 500.0) and engine hours start 820.3
confirmedRules.and: On save, the flight's UsedMeterOffset is taken from the flight key info for new flights, but from the displayed label for existing flights (lines 477-481)
edgeCases: Engine hours start is only defaulted when an aircraft has been chosen (AircraftId <> 0)
In edit mode the stored values are shown instead of recomputed defaults (lines 411-421)

confirmedRules.name: Liquid fill airframe-hours reading derived from Hobbs reading
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Each fuel/oil/liquid fill records the Hobbs reading at the time of fill and an airframe-hours reading equal to that Hobbs reading plus the aircraft's meter offset; if no Hobbs reading is entered, it defaults to the aircraft's current airframe hours minus the offset.
confirmedRules.given: A flight on an aircraft with meter offset 500.0 and current airframe hours 1,736.0
confirmedRules.when: A liquid fill row is added with Hobbs reading 1,235.2
confirmedRules.then: The fill is stored with Hobbs reading 1,235.2 and airframe hours reading 1,735.2
confirmedRules.and: If the Hobbs reading is left blank, the Hobbs reading stored is 1,236.0 (1,736.0 - 500.0)
confirmedRules.parameters: Offset = FlightKeyInfo.AirframeHoursOffset; mask '#,##0.0;-#,##0.0'
edgeCases: Blank Hobbs on add: airframeHoursReading variable stays 0 and is stored as 0.0 even though the Hobbs reading is defaulted (lines 544-547, 569)
A fill row is only created if at least one of group, type, unit, amount, Hobbs, location or approver is entered (lines 551-552)
On row update, the airframe hours reading is recomputed as Hobbs + offset (line 599)
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: When the Hobbs reading on a liquid fill is left blank, should the airframe-hours reading be the aircraft's current airframe hours (consistent with the defaulted Hobbs) rather than 0.0?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: On add with blank Hobbs, AirframeHoursReading is saved as 0.0 instead of defaulted Hobbs + offset. On update (lines 595-599), the default-Hobbs branch tests whether the liquid AMOUNT is numeric, uses current hours without subtracting the offset, and is then immediately overwritten by the textbox value, so a blank Hobbs causes CDec('') to fail.

confirmedRules.name: One flight per aircraft, location, date and work shift

confirmedRules.then: The page shows 'This flight already exists!' with options Edit, Retry, Cancel and does not open the new-flight form
confirmedRules.and: If the key lookup returns validation errors, the message 'Unable to retrieve information. Please correct errors and try again.' is shown and the form does not advance
confirmedRules.parameters: Key = (AircraftId, LocationId, FlightDateSort, WorkShiftId) resolved by FlightKeyInfoManager.GetItem
edgeCases: Edit loads the existing flight by FlightKeyInfo.FlightId and switches page to edit mode (lines 182-200)
Retry re-shows Next and hides Edit/Retry (lines 202-208)
Uniqueness determination (ValidFlight) is computed in the business layer, not in this page

confirmedRules.name: Fleet pages require a logged-in session scoped to the current program
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: All fleet pages require a logged-in user and scope all data to the user's current program.

edgeCases: Other pages check both Nothing and IsLoggedIn (e.g., FlightModify.aspx.vb:24-28)

confirmedRules.name: Program reference data needs a logged-in user and is scoped to that user's current program
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Every program-setup screen sends anonymous users to the login page, and all lists and new records are tied to the program the user is currently working in.
confirmedRules.given: A user whose session identity has CurrentProgId = 7
confirmedRules.when: they open Locations, Routes, Regions, Weight Tracking, Configuration Values or Program Profile
confirmedRules.then: only records for program 7 are listed, and any new Location, Region, Route, Weight definition or lookup value is stamped with ProgId 7. A missing or logged-out session goes to ~/Login.aspx.
confirmedRules.parameters: Session key 'fltIdentity'; redirect target ~/Login.aspx; ProgId comes from FltIdentity.CurrentProgId through ProgIdHiddenField
edgeCases: The same gate is repeated in ConfigValues.aspx.vb:12-25, Regions.aspx.vb:18-30, Routes.aspx.vb:18-31, WeightDefs.aspx.vb:17-30 and ProgramProfile.aspx.vb:45-56
ProgramProfile loads the program by CurrentProgId, so a user can only edit their current program
The `Or` is not short-circuiting, so a null session reads _fltIdentity.IsLoggedIn and throws a NullReferenceException instead of redirecting
The ProgId sits in a client-side hidden field, so a tampered postback could write records to another program
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: `(_fltIdentity Is Nothing) Or (_fltIdentity.IsLoggedIn = False)` uses a non-short-circuit Or, so an expired session crashes instead of redirecting. Program scoping also relies on a client-editable hidden field (ProgIdHiddenField) and not on the server-side identity.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion:
P0 panel doubts spec fidelity: P0 is justified. This is the login and program-scoping gate for every program reference-data screen. It keeps one program's locations, routes, regions, weight definitions and config values separate from another's. If that changed without notice, records could leak across programs or be written to the wrong one. An auditor would care about that as a security and data-integrity control. The Given/When/Then is not faithful on two points:

(1) The check at FLTWebApp/program/locations.aspx.vb:20 uses VB `Or`, which does not short-circuit. The same pattern appears in ConfigValues.aspx.vb:14, ProgramProfile.aspx.vb:47, Regions, Routes and WeightDefs. When Session("fltIdentity") is Nothing, evaluating `_fltIdentity.IsLoggedIn` throws a NullReferenceException before Response.Redirect runs. Global.asax.vb:34 has an empty Application_Error, and Web.config:16 sets customErrors mode="Off". So a missing session ends in an unhandled error, not a redirect to ~/Login.aspx. Only an identity that exists with IsLoggedIn=False is redirected.

(2) The claim that new Routes are stamped with ProgId 7 has no support. Routes.aspx.vb creates `New Route` at line 106 and saves it at line 126, but never assigns ProgId. Locations (157), Regions (142), WeightDefs (187) and ConfigValues (116) do assign it from ProgIdHiddenField.

Smaller points: ProgramProfile reads CurrentProgId directly instead of through ProgIdHiddenField. ProgId is kept in a client-side hidden field that is reset on every Page_Load, so this is UI-level scoping. The business layer may not enforce it on its own. | P0 is justified. This rule is the authentication gate and the per-program data boundary for all program reference data. If it is wrong, users see or write another program's data, which is a security and data-integrity failure.

The Given/When/Then does not match the code in three places:

1. **A missing session does not go to the login page.** At locations.aspx.vb:20 the check is `(_fltIdentity Is Nothing) Or (_fltIdentity.IsLoggedIn = False)`. VB's `Or` evaluates both sides, so when Session("fltIdentity") is Nothing the second side throws a NullReferenceException before Response.Redirect runs. The same pattern is at ConfigValues.aspx.vb:14, Regions.aspx.vb:20, Routes.aspx.vb:20, WeightDefs.aspx.vb:19 and ProgramProfile.aspx.vb:47. Only a session that exists with IsLoggedIn = False reaches ~/Login.aspx. The spec's claim that "a missing ... session goes to ~/Login.aspx" is wrong.

2. **New Routes are not stamped with the program.** Locations (locations.aspx.vb:157), Regions (Regions.aspx.vb:142), WeightDefs (WeightDefs.aspx.vb:187) and ConfigValues (ConfigValues.aspx.vb:116) set ProgId from ProgIdHiddenField. Routes.aspx.vb never assigns ProgId. AddButton_Click creates a new Route and SaveButton_Click calls RouteManager.Save with no ProgId set, so the spec's claim that new Routes get ProgId 7 has no support in this code.

3. **Program Profile is not scoped through the hidden field.** It reads _fltIdentity.CurrentProgId directly (ProgramProfile.aspx.vb:51) and edits that one program record. The hidden-field mechanism in the Parameters does not apply to it.

What does hold: Page_Load overwrites ProgIdHiddenField from CurrentProgId on every request (locations.aspx.vb:23), and the list queries filter by that value (locations.aspx.vb:38, and the matching lines in the other pages). Edit and delete fetch records by ID with GetItem(id, _fltIdentity) and do not check that the record belongs to the current program. An SME should confirm whether the manager layer enforces that.

The cited lines contain no instruction-shaped text and no credentials.

confirmedRules.smeQuestion: P0 panel split on whether this is critical to the system's core purpose or a costly-if-wrong rule (Faithful: at FLTWebApp/reports/rptWeightTracking.aspx.vb:33-38 the click handler takes progId straight from the session (_fltIdentity.CurrentProgId, line 36). Two details are left out but don't change the rule: the export only includes active, non-deleted weight definitions (IsActiveFilter=1, IsDeletedFilter=0), and the user must pass the CanView check. P0 is justified from a compliance view. The rule keeps each program's data separate in a bulk export, which is a security and data-integrity boundary. If a rewrite quietly let a user pick the program, or dropped the filter, one program's data would leak to users of another program in a downloadable file. An auditor would see that as a data-segregation breach, and it can't be undone once the file is downloaded. The same pattern is repeated across all six report pages, which makes it a system-wide behavior every modernization phase must prove still holds. One caveat for SMEs: ChangeCurrentProgram (FLTBizObjects/BusinessLogic/fltIdentityManager.vb:83-94) sets CurrentProgId to NewProgId and only looks it up in UserProgramsList to set the display name. It never rejects a program the user isn't assigned to. The isolation therefore relies on callers passing only programs the user is assigned to. I found no injection-style text in the cited lines. | Fidelity: the rule matches the code. In FLTWebApp/reports/rptWeightTracking.aspx.vb:36-38, DownloadDataButton_Click reads progId from _fltIdentity.CurrentProgId, which comes from the session, and passes it to RptWeightTrackingManager.GetSpreadsheet(_fltIdentity, progId). The page has no control for picking a program. In FLTBizObjects/BusinessLogic/RptWeightTrackingManager.vb:19, GetSpreadsheet passes ProgId on to WeightDefDB.GetList, so the export is filtered to that program. The Given/When/Then leaves out some edge cases. GetSpreadsheet first runs a CanView check and throws "User is not authorized" if it fails (line 14). The export only includes active, non-deleted weight definitions (IsActiveFilter=1, IsDeletedFilter=0). If the list is empty, the page shows the error "No information retrieved" (lines 40-41) instead of downloading a file. The file name uses the current program's ProgName (line 44). None of these contradict the stated rule. P0: not justified. The cited code only connects the session's program to one report query. It does not check that the user is allowed to use that program. That check, which is what actually keeps one program's data away from another, sits where CurrentProgId is set (program selection, FLT.Master.vb) and in CanView, not here. The data exported is weight-definition configuration, not money, regulatory data or the system's central flight-log decision. Program scoping is a pattern repeated across many report pages, and this page is one example of it. A tenancy or program-isolation rule tied to where CurrentProgId is set and validated could deserve P0, but this page-level wiring card does not. No instruction-shaped text was found in the cited lines.) — confirm criticality.

confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Every user, role, module, permission and profile page sends anyone without a logged-in session to the login page. Beyond that, the pages run no role or module permission check of their own.

edgeCases: No server-side Security/CanEdit authorization on any page: a non-admin who knows the URL can create users, grant super user, and change permissions
The non-short-circuit 'Or' evaluates _fltIdentity.IsLoggedIn even when _fltIdentity Is Nothing
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: 1) VB 'Or' does not short-circuit, so a missing session throws a NullReferenceException instead of redirecting (OrElse was intended). 2) Admin pages check only that the user is logged in, not the 'Security' module permission, so access depends on the menu link being hidden.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion:
P0 panel doubts spec fidelity: P0 is justified. This is the authentication gate on the user, role, module and permission administration pages, so it is a security and access-control rule. Getting it wrong lets someone take over accounts or raise their own privileges.

The Given/When/Then is not faithful, for two reasons.

(1) The cited guard at FLTWebApp/security/users.aspx.vb:19-21 uses VB `Or`, not `OrElse`, so it does not short-circuit. When Session("fltIdentity") Is Nothing, `_fltIdentity.IsLoggedIn` is still evaluated and throws a NullReferenceException. The user is not redirected to ~/Login.aspx. Global.asax.vb:23-26 normally fills the session with a new, not-logged-in FltIdentity, so the IsLoggedIn = False case does redirect. But FLTWebApp/export/autoUtilityProcs.vb:20 sets Session("fltIdentity") = Nothing, and in that case the page fails with an exception. Global.asax.vb Application_Error is empty and Web.config:16 has customErrors mode="Off". The card says "no fltIdentity -> redirected", which is wrong for this edge case. The same pattern is in all six pages listed.

(2) The claim that "any logged-in user who reaches the URL directly can use all admin functions" is overstated. The pages themselves do not call AuthorizeUserAction, but the business layer enforces the 'Security' module permissions. FLTBizObjects/BusinessLogic/FltRoleManager.vb:20-28 and 44-99 check CanView or CanEdit before every list, get, insert, update and delete, and throw "user is not authorized" otherwise. FltModuleManager.vb:102-106, FltRoleModulePermissionsManager.vb:115-119 and FltUserInRoleManager.vb:92-96 have the same checks. Only FltUserManager (FLTBizObjects/BusinessLogic/FltUserManager.vb:39-91: Save, Update, Insert, Delete and UnlockUserAccount) has no permission check. So the gap is real for user create, edit, delete and unlock on users.aspx, but not for the roles, modules or role-module-permission pages.

The rest of the card is accurate: the session key 'fltIdentity', the ~/Login.aspx redirect target, the duplicated checks in the listed files (the profile pages are in FLTWebApp/userProfile/), and the fact that FLT.Master.vb:101 only hides the menu.

The fleet endpoint subtracts the offset while the flight endpoint adds it. | Citation was corrected by referee (The rule is real, but the citation points at the wrong lines. Lines 114-115 only copy AircraftGUID and CurrentLocationId into the response object. They do no hours calculation. The calculation appears in two places in FleetController.cs. Line 96 (list mapper, takes AircraftInfo) and line 121 (item mapper, takes FLT.BO.Aircraft) both set AirframeHoursCurrent = Convert.ToDecimal(AirframeHoursCurrent) - Convert.ToDecimal(AirframeHoursOffset). Lines 97 and 122 then pass AirframeHoursOffset through unchanged. This is executable code, not a comment, so the formula and the example in the rule (1622.1 - 1500.0 = 122.1, offset 1500.0) both hold. No instruction-shaped text appears in the cited region.) — confirm FLTWebAPI/FltWebApi/Controllers/FleetController.cs:96-97,121-122 is the authoritative implementation.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The offset is applied in opposite directions (subtracted for Aircraft, added for Flight). The field named AirframeHoursCurrent may actually return the meter reading, which could mislead clients that use it to pre-fill HobbsStart or to check maintenance hours.

confirmedRules.name: Flight load configuration: one airframe, up to two cargo items, one ballast
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Each flight records exactly one airframe configuration, at most two cargo loads (Cargo1, Cargo2) and one ballast item, each picked from a reference list with a description, weight and weight unit.
confirmedRules.given: A flight that carries three distinct cargo items
confirmedRules.then: Only two cargo references (Cargo1Id, Cargo2Id) can be stored; a third cannot be recorded
confirmedRules.parameters: Max cargo slots per flight = 2 (Cargo1Id, Cargo2Id). Reference catalogs: Airframes (Airframe.cs:11-17), Cargos (Cargo.cs:11-17), Dollies/Ballast (Ballast.cs:11-17).
edgeCases: Ids are non-nullable ints, so 'no cargo' must be shown by a sentinel value (probably 0)
The ballast collection is serialized as 'Dollies', which suggests ballast means ground dollies
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is the two-cargo limit a real business limit or a schema convenience? What value means 'no cargo/ballast' (0)? Are 'Ballast' and 'Dollies' the same concept?

confirmedRules.name: Weights are free-text with a separate unit (not validated as numbers)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Airframe, cargo and ballast weights are stored as text along with a separate weight-unit text, so the API does not enforce numeric weights or a standard unit.
confirmedRules.given: A cargo item with Weight '12O' (letter O) and WeightUnit 'lbs'
confirmedRules.when: It is returned by the reference-data API
confirmedRules.then: The value is passed through unchanged; no numeric or unit check is applied
confirmedRules.parameters: Same layout in Cargo.cs:13-16 and Ballast.cs:13-16.
edgeCases: Mixed units (lb/kg) across items cannot be summed without conversion
Any total-weight or weight-and-balance calculation would have to parse text
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Are weights used in any weight-and-balance or total-load calculation downstream? If so, what units are allowed and how are they converted?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Storing weights as strings with no validation can let malformed weights into any load calculation.

confirmedRules.name: Pre-flight and post-flight checklist results recorded per flight
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Each flight records the pre-flight checks (FTI OK, telemetry OK, telemetry check complete, starting oil and hydraulic levels) and post-flight checks (FTI OK, telemetry check complete, nacelle build-up, nacelle discoloration) as small-integer flags.
confirmedRules.given: A flight whose PreFlightTelemetryOK is 0 (not OK)
confirmedRules.when: The flight is saved through the API
confirmedRules.then: The flight is stored anyway; the model has no rule that blocks departure or flags the flight because a check failed
confirmedRules.parameters: Pre-flight: PreFlightFtiOK, PreFlightTelemetryOK, PreFlightTelemetryCheckComplete, OilLevelIndicatorStart, HydraulicLevelIndicatorStart. Post-flight: PostFlightFtiOK, PostFlightTelemetryCheckComplete, NacelleCheckBuildUp, NacelleCheckDiscoloration. All are type short.
edgeCases: Oil and hydraulic level indicators are shorts, which may be level codes rather than booleans
Nacelle checks may encode severity, not just pass/fail
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: What values are valid for each checklist field (0/1 boolean, or a graded scale for oil/hydraulic level and nacelle condition)? Must a failed pre-flight check block or flag the flight?

confirmedRules.name: Flight records both scheduled and actually flown route
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A flight is logged for an aircraft at a location by an evaluator on a flight date and work shift, and records both the scheduled route and the route actually flown so that deviations can be seen.
confirmedRules.given: A flight scheduled on route 'R1' that actually flew route 'R2'
confirmedRules.then: SchedRouteId points to R1 and FlownRouteId points to R2
confirmedRules.parameters: Route catalog: Route.cs:11-16. WorkShiftIndicatorId is a lookup value (LookUpValue.cs:11-16). FlightDate, DepartureTime and ReturnTime are strings.
edgeCases: Dates and times are strings, so ReturnTime after DepartureTime is not enforced at the model level
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is a scheduled-vs-flown route mismatch reported or checked anywhere, and must ReturnTime be after DepartureTime?

confirmedRules.name: Liquid fills recorded with Hobbs reading and approver
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Each fluid replenishment on a flight records its type and subtype, amount and unit, the Hobbs reading when it was done, where it was done, and who approved it.
confirmedRules.given: A 2.5-quart oil top-up at Hobbs 1,235.2
confirmedRules.when: It is added to a flight's LiquidFills
confirmedRules.then: It is stored with LiquidAmt 2.5, LiquidUnitId = quarts, HobbsReading 1,235.2, plus location and approver name
confirmedRules.parameters: LiquidFillTypeId, LiquidFillSubTypeId and LiquidUnitId are lookup ids; the approver is free text.
edgeCases: Nothing at the model level requires an approver
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is an approver mandatory for every liquid fill (or for certain fluid types)? Should the fill's Hobbs reading fall between the flight's HobbsStart and HobbsEnd?

confirmedRules.name: Flight time split across operating regions
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A flight's time is broken down into hours spent in each operating region.
confirmedRules.given: A 1.5-hour flight with 1.0 hours in region 'N' and 0.5 hours in region 'S'
confirmedRules.then: Two RegionTime rows are stored (1.0 and 0.5 hours); the model does not check that they add up to the flight duration
confirmedRules.parameters: Region catalog: Region.cs:11-16 (Id, Code, Name). Flight.RegionTimes collection: Flight.cs:53.
edgeCases: Hours are decimals with no stated precision
Region hours may not match HobbsEnd - HobbsStart
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Must the sum of RegionTime hours equal the flight's Hobbs duration (HobbsEnd - HobbsStart), and to what precision?

confirmedRules.name: Evaluator comments carry component, issue code and rating
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Evaluator comments on a flight are tied to a component and an issue code, carry a time and a numeric rating, and engine runs record engine speed with start and end times.
confirmedRules.given: An evaluator notes vibration on component 12 with issue code 3
confirmedRules.when: The comment is added to the flight
confirmedRules.then: A FlightComment is stored with ComponentId 12, IssueCodeId 3, the comment text, the time and a CommentRating
confirmedRules.parameters: CommentRating is a short with an unspecified scale. EngineRun (EngineRun.cs:11-17) has EngineSpeed (int), RunStartTime and RunEndTime (strings).
edgeCases: The rating scale is not defined in code
EngineRun times are strings, so end-after-start is not checked
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: What is the CommentRating scale and what does each value mean (for example, severity)? Is there a valid range for EngineSpeed?

confirmedRules.name: Locations belong to a test program
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Every operating location belongs to one program, so locations, and the aircraft and flights at them, can be scoped by program.
confirmedRules.given: Location 'Site A' with ProgId 4
confirmedRules.then: Site A is linked to program 4 (Program.cs: ProgID, name, description, version)
confirmedRules.parameters: Program catalog: Program.cs:11-17.
edgeCases: Aircraft.CurrentLocationId and Flight.LocationId link aircraft and flights to locations, and through them to programs
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Are users or flights limited to locations within their program?

confirmedRules.name: Duplicate flight entry check (aircraft + location + date + shift)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Only one flight log may exist per aircraft, per location, per flight date, per work shift; a second one is reported as a 'Duplicate Flight Entry'.
confirmedRules.given: Aircraft 12 already has a non-deleted flight at location 3 on FlightDateSort '2024-05-14' for work shift 1
confirmedRules.when: addFlight is called with AircraftId 12, LocationId 3, FlightDateSort '2024-05-14', WorkShiftIndicatorId 1
confirmedRules.then: the error 'Duplicate Flight Entry' (severity 16) is raised. Because there is no RETURN after it, the INSERT still runs unless the caller rolls back.
confirmedRules.parameters: Uniqueness key = AircraftId, LocationId, FlightDateSort, WorkShiftIndicatorId among rows with IsDeleted = 0. Error severity 16. Original location: database/FLT_Schema.sql:3847-3855 (addFlight).
edgeCases: Soft-deleted flights (IsDeleted = 1) do not count, so a deleted flight can be re-entered.
Inactive but not deleted flights (IsActive = 0) still count as duplicates.
updateFlight (excerpt lines 1128-1272) does not repeat this check, so an edit can move a flight onto an existing aircraft/location/date/shift slot.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: RAISERROR at severity 16 does not stop the procedure and there is no RETURN, so execution goes on to the INSERT. Whether the duplicate is actually blocked depends on how the caller handles the error (transaction rollback or not). | RAISERROR with severity 16 does not stop the batch, and there is no RETURN or ROLLBACK, so the INSERT at lines 77-169 still runs. The caller gets an error, but the duplicate flight is saved anyway (and an approved one also updates the aircraft hours).
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Does the calling application wrap addFlight in a transaction and roll back when 'Duplicate Flight Entry' is raised, or do duplicate flight rows actually get saved today? Also, should updateFlight enforce the same uniqueness rule? | Should a duplicate flight be hard-blocked with no insert? Should soft-deleted or inactive flights count toward the duplicate check?

confirmedRules.name: Flight approval stamping (who approved and when)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When a flight that was not yet approved is saved as approved, the system records the saving user as the approver and the current UTC time as the approval date.
confirmedRules.given: Flight 501 is stored with IsApproved = 0 and user 'jsmith' saves it with IsApproved = 1
confirmedRules.then: ApprovedBy = 'jsmith' and UTCDateApproved = the current UTC time, whatever values the caller passed
confirmedRules.parameters: States: IsApproved 0 (pending) to 1 (approved). Original location: database/FLT_Schema.sql:17284-17301; values persisted at 17341-17343.
edgeCases: Re-saving an already-approved flight keeps the caller-supplied ApprovedBy and UTCDateApproved. If the caller omits them, the defaults ('' and NULL) erase the original approver and date.
Un-approving (IsApproved = 0) is allowed with no restriction and stores whatever ApprovedBy and UTCDateApproved the caller passes.

addFlight (excerpt lines 43-45, 148-150) takes IsApproved, ApprovedBy and UtcDateApproved straight from the caller with no server-side stamping, so a flight created as approved can carry any approver name.
There is no role or authorization check on who may approve.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Approval audit fields can be overwritten or cleared on later edits, and creating a flight as approved bypasses server-side stamping.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Who is allowed to approve or un-approve a flight log, and must the original approver and date be kept when an approved flight is edited later?

confirmedRules.name: Flight record status flags and visibility
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A new flight is created active, not deleted, with a new GUID and created/modified timestamps. Flights are soft-deleted, and only active, non-deleted flights count in reports and aircraft totals.
confirmedRules.given: A user creates a flight
confirmedRules.then: IsActive = 1, a new FlightGuid is assigned, UTCDateCreated = UTCDateModified = now (UTC), and StampUserName = the caller
confirmedRules.parameters: Flags: IsActive (1 = active), IsDeleted (soft delete; not set by addFlight, so presumably 0 by column default), IsApproved. Original location: database/FLT_Schema.sql:3944-3948.
edgeCases: updateFlight can set IsActive to 0 or 1, but none of these procedures sets IsDeleted (deletion is done elsewhere).
rptFlightOutliers does not filter on IsActive or IsDeleted (see the outlier rule).
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: What is the business difference between an inactive flight (IsActive = 0) and a deleted flight (IsDeleted = 1), and which procedure sets IsDeleted?

confirmedRules.name: Flight log search filters and defaults
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The flight list hides deleted flights by default, shows approved and unapproved, active and inactive flights unless filtered, treats 0 or an empty value as 'no filter', and matches aircraft text against serial, registration, MSN or ship number.
confirmedRules.given: No filters are supplied except AircraftTextMatch 'N12%'
confirmedRules.then: every non-deleted flight dated 1900-01-01 through 2100-12-31 whose aircraft SerialNbr, RegistrationNbr, MSN or ShipNbr is LIKE 'N12%' is returned, ordered by MSN, then AirframeHoursEnd descending, then FlightDateSort descending
confirmedRules.parameters: Tri-state filters: 1 = only true, 0 = only false, -1 = all. Defaults: IsApprovedFilter -1, IsActiveFilter -1, IsDeletedFilter 0. Default date range 1900-01-01 to 2100-12-31. Original location: database/FLT_Schema.sql:12326-12387.
edgeCases: @Start, @Count and @Total are declared but never used, so there is no paging and @Total is never set.
The date filter converts the varchar FlightDate to a DATETIME, so an unparseable stored date makes the query fail.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Paging parameters (@Start, @Count) and the @Total output are accepted but ignored.

confirmedRules.name: Flight usage hours per flight
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A flight's usage (daily hours) is the airframe hours end reading minus the start reading, except in the flight list and the outlier report, which use the Hobbs meter difference.
confirmedRules.given: A flight with AirframeHoursStart 1500.2, AirframeHoursEnd 1503.7, HobbsStart 900.0 and HobbsEnd 903.4
confirmedRules.then: DailyHours = 3.5. listFlightInfos FlightUsage and the rptFlightOutliers airtime = 3.4 (Hobbs).
confirmedRules.parameters: Airframe basis: rptFlightData (original database/FLT_Schema.sql:15051) and rptDailyUsage (excerpt 395, 423, 446). Hobbs basis: listFlightInfos (excerpt 240; original 12355) and rptFlightOutliers (excerpt 1048, 1084).
edgeCases: There is no guard that the end reading is at least the start reading, so negative usage is possible.
UsedMeterOffset is stored but never used in any usage calculation.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Two different meters (airframe hours and Hobbs) are both labelled 'usage' or 'airtime', so screens and reports can disagree for the same flight.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Which meter is the authoritative measure of flight usage, airframe hours or Hobbs, and what is UsedMeterOffset meant to adjust?

confirmedRules.name: Daily usage report: aircraft assigned to a location on a date
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: An active aircraft in the program counts as being at a test location on the report date if the assignment's actual end-of-test is on or after that date, or (when there is no actual end) its estimated end-of-test is on or after that date, or the assignment has no end date at all. If an aircraft has several qualifying assignments, the one ending soonest is meant to be used.
confirmedRules.given: Aircraft 12 has assignment A at location 3 with ActEndOfTest 2024-06-30, and assignment B at location 4 with no ActEndOfTest and EstEndOfTest 2024-07-15
confirmedRules.then: as written, only assignment A qualifies (B is dropped by the NULL-comparison bug), and A's EndTestDate shows as NULL
confirmedRules.parameters: @LocationId -1 = all locations. Only aircraft with IsDeleted = 0 and IsActive = 1 in @ProgId. Original location: database/FLT_Schema.sql:14306-14365.
edgeCases: Assignments with no actual and no estimated end date are always included.
The 'earliest end date per aircraft' step compares EndTestDate values that are always NULL, so every qualifying assignment is kept and an aircraft at several locations appears on several rows.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Lines 312 and 314 use '<> NULL' and line 330 uses 'NOT (EstEndOfTest = NULL)'. Under ANSI_NULLS these never evaluate true, so (1) EndTestDate / LocationEndTestDate is always NULL and (2) assignments that have only an estimated end-of-test date are excluded. The 'pick the earliest-ending assignment' logic therefore never takes effect.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should an assignment with only an estimated end-of-test date on or after the report date count as active, and should the report show one row per aircraft (soonest-ending assignment) or one per location?

confirmedRules.name: Location and program test-completion percentage
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Location progress is the aircraft's cumulative flight hours at that location up to the report date as a percentage of the location's required usage. Program progress is the aircraft's cumulative hours across its qualifying locations as a percentage of its total required usage. A missing or zero goal gives 0%.
confirmedRules.given: Aircraft 12 at location 3 has RequiredUsage 200.0 h and active flights there up to 2024-05-14 totalling 50.0 airframe hours, and Aircraft.TotalRequiredUsage 400.0 h with 120.0 h total across qualifying locations
confirmedRules.then: LocationPercentComplete = 25.0 (100 × 50.0 / 200.0) and ProgramPercentComplete = 30.0 (100 × 120.0 / 400.0)
confirmedRules.parameters: Formula: 100 × SUM(AirframeHoursEnd − AirframeHoursStart) / goal, returned as FLOAT with no rounding. Goal 0 or NULL gives 0. Flights counted: FlightDate <= report date, IsDeleted = 0, IsActive = 1. Also LastMeterReading = MAX(AirframeHoursEnd), falling back to Aircraft.AirframeHoursStart; HoursOnDate = airframe end − start for the flight on the report date (0 if none); DateLastRun = MAX(FlightDateSort). Original location: database/FLT_Schema.sql:14383-14471.
edgeCases: Program-level usage only counts flights at locations in the qualifying-assignment set, not all of the aircraft's flights.
If an aircraft has two qualifying assignment rows for the same location, the join doubles its flight hours.
An aircraft linked to several tests, or with several flights on the report date at one location, produces duplicate rows.
Aircraft linked to an inactive test are excluded entirely; aircraft with no test show 'None Assigned'.
Percentages can exceed 100.
ProgramEndTestDate is just Aircraft.EstEndOfTesting.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Program percent complete is limited to hours at currently qualifying locations, so hours flown at earlier, ended assignments are left out. That understates program progress.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should program-level completion count all of the aircraft's approved and active flight hours, regardless of which location assignment is currently active?

confirmedRules.name: Fuel/liquid usage per refill interval
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: For each refill of the selected liquid, the hours flown since the previous refill are divided by the amount added to give hours per unit of liquid. The refill meter reading is the airframe-hours reading, or the Hobbs reading when no airframe reading was recorded.
confirmedRules.given: The previous refill of aircraft 12 was at meter 1500.0 and a new fuel fill of 40.000 units is logged with AirframeHoursReading 1504.0
confirmedRules.then: RefillAirtime = 4.0 and Usage = 4.0 / 40.000 = 0.100 hours per unit, and the refill baseline moves to 1504.0
confirmedRules.parameters: Refill meter = AirframeHoursReading if non-zero, else HobbsReading. Usage = (RefillMeterCurrent − RefillMeterLast) / LiquidAmt, 0 if LiquidAmt = 0. Only fills with LiquidGroupId = @LiquidGroupId, IsDeleted = 0 and IsActive = 1. The baseline for an aircraft's first refill is the FlightMeterStart (AirframeHoursStart) of its first flight. Original location: database/FLT_Schema.sql:14855-14943.
edgeCases: If a flight has several fills, the flight start/end/airtime columns are NULL on the second and later fill rows, so the flight is not double counted.
Flights with no fill still produce a row with flight airtime and no refill data.
If both refill readings are 0, the current meter is 0 and the refill interval goes negative.
LiquidAmt is held as DECIMAL(6,3) in #flights and the cursor variable, so amounts of 1000 or more overflow.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: 'Usage' is hours per unit of liquid (inverse burn rate), not liquid consumed per hour as the report name 'Fuel Burn' suggests. LiquidAmt DECIMAL(6,3) overflows for fills of 1,000 or more.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should the report express fuel burn as liquid per hour (amount / hours) or as hours per unit of liquid as it does today?

confirmedRules.name: Fuel burn running totals and average per aircraft
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Per aircraft, the report keeps running totals of flight airtime, refill-interval airtime and liquid added, and computes an average of total refill airtime divided by total liquid. All totals restart when the aircraft changes.
confirmedRules.given: Aircraft 12 has refills covering 4.0 h with 40 units and 6.0 h with 50 units, and the report date range starts after the first refill
confirmedRules.then: the second fill row shows TotalRefillAirtime 10.0, TotalLiquidAmt 90.000 and AvgUsage 0.111 (10.0 / 90). Running totals include history before DateFrom because the date filter is applied only to the final output.
confirmedRules.parameters: Reset on aircraft change: RefillMeterLast = the new aircraft's first FlightMeterStart, and all totals = 0. AvgUsage = TotalRefillAirtime / TotalLiquidAmt, 0 if total = 0, stored as DECIMAL(6,3). Output filtered to FlightDate between @DateFrom and @DateThru (excerpt 891-892; original database/FLT_Schema.sql:15011-15012). @AircraftId -1 = all aircraft in the program.
edgeCases: The date filter is applied after accumulation, so totals and averages are lifetime-to-date rather than period-only.
Rows are inserted ordered by HobbsStart, but the cursor processes them ordered by FlightDate, FlightMeterStart and AirframeHoursReading, which can differ.
The flight-level filters ignore Program.IsActive and only check IsDeleted.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should the totals and average cover only the selected date range or lifetime-to-date as now?

confirmedRules.name: Flight data report: liquids per flight and record eligibility
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The flight data report lists each active, non-deleted flight of an active program with its daily hours and the total fuel, oil and other fluids added on that flight (active, non-deleted fills only), filtered optionally by location, aircraft and date range.
confirmedRules.given: Flight 501 has active fuel fills of 20 and 15 units and one oil fill of 1.5 units
confirmedRules.when: rptFlightData runs with the fuel and oil group ids
confirmedRules.then: Fuel = 35, Oil = 1.5, Fluids = 0, and DailyHours = AirframeHoursEnd − AirframeHoursStart
confirmedRules.parameters: Filter 0 or NULL = no filter for LocationId, AircraftId, DateRangeStart and DateRangeEnd (inclusive). Liquid groups are passed in as @FuelLiquidGroupId, @OilLiquidGroupId and @FluidsLiquidGroupId. Original location: database/FLT_Schema.sql:15074-15095.
edgeCases: A flight with several comments appears once per comment.
Missing liquid amounts show as 0, and a missing comment shows as an empty string with rating 0.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Line 975 checks 'V.IsDeleted = 0 AND P.IsActive = 1', which repeats the program check instead of checking Aircraft.IsActive, so flights of inactive aircraft appear in the report.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should flights of inactive (but not deleted) aircraft be excluded from the flight data report?

confirmedRules.name: Flight outlier detection by standard deviation
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A flight is flagged as an outlier when its duration in minutes, or its Hobbs airtime, is greater than the average for its location, flown route and meter unit plus N standard deviations, where N is supplied by the user.
confirmedRules.given: Location 3, route 7, meter unit 1 has average flight time 120 min with standard deviation 15, and average airtime 2.0 with standard deviation 0.3; N = 2
confirmedRules.when: a flight in the date range lasted 155 minutes with Hobbs airtime 2.4
confirmedRules.then: FlightTimeOutlier = 1 (155 > 150), FlightAirtimeOutlier = 0 (2.4 <= 2.6), and the flight is listed
confirmedRules.parameters: Threshold = AVG + @NbrOfStDevs × STDEV, with STDEV NULL treated as 0. Minute statistics are stored as INT, so they truncate. Group = route's LocationId, FlownRouteId, MeterUnitId. Date range is FlightDateSort between @DateBegin and @DateEnd as string comparison. Original location: database/FLT_Schema.sql:15144-15233.
edgeCases: Only unusually long or high values are flagged; unusually short flights are never outliers (one-sided test, ABS of a positive duration).
A group with a single flight has STDEV 0, so the threshold equals that flight's own value and it is not flagged.
Statistics are grouped by the route's location, but flights are matched by the flight's own LocationId.
Statistics filter on the program via Aircraft.ProgId, but the output filters via Location.ProgId.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Neither the statistics nor the output filter on Flight.IsDeleted or IsActive, so deleted or inactive flights skew the averages and can be reported as outliers. Truncating average and stdev minutes to INT shifts the threshold.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should deleted or inactive flights be excluded from outlier statistics, and should unusually short flights also be flagged?

confirmedRules.name: Login credential and account-status check
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A user can log in only when the user name and password match one account (ignoring upper/lower case), and that account is approved, active, not deleted and not locked out.
confirmedRules.given: FltUser 'JSMITH' has a stored password, IsApproved=1, IsActive=1, IsDeleted=0, IsLockedOut=0
confirmedRules.when: fltValidateLogin is called with UserName 'jsmith' and the same password typed in a different letter case
confirmedRules.then: Exactly 1 row matches, so login succeeds and the profile and program result sets are returned. If any flag fails (for example IsLockedOut=1), or the count is not exactly 1, no result set is returned and the caller treats the login as failed.
confirmedRules.parameters: Original source database/FLT_Schema.sql:6743-6753. Required flags: IsApproved=1, IsActive=1, IsDeleted=0, IsLockedOut=0. Match count must equal 1. UserName NVARCHAR(20), Password NVARCHAR(128). No credential values in code.
edgeCases: Both user name and password are compared with LOWER(), so 'Secret' and 'SECRET' are treated as the same password
If two accounts match (duplicate user names that differ only in case), the count is 2 and login fails silently
When login fails, nothing is written: FailedPasswordAttemptCount is not incremented and no lockout is set in this procedure
PasswordSalt exists on FltUser but is not used in the comparison
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The password is compared as plain text and the comparison ignores letter case (LOWER on both sides). That means passwords are stored unhashed, or the salt is ignored, and password strength is reduced. Failed attempts are never counted here, so the lockout flag cannot be triggered by this path.

confirmedRules.name: Successful login records last-login time
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: After a successful login, the system returns the user's display name, default program, previous last-login date and super-user flag, then stamps the current UTC time as the user's new last-login date.
confirmedRules.given: User 'jsmith' passed the credential check, with utcLastLoginDate 2026-10-01 08:00 UTC and DefaultProgId 3 ('Program A')
confirmedRules.then: The returned profile shows LastLoginDate 2026-10-01 08:00 (the previous value), DefaultProgName 'Program A', and utcLastLoginDate is updated to 2026-10-15 14:00
confirmedRules.parameters: Original source database/FLT_Schema.sql:6753-6771. The timestamp is GETUTCDATE().
edgeCases: A missing default program returns DefaultProgName '' (LEFT JOIN + ISNULL)
A null last-login date returns '' through ISNULL, which SQL Server converts to 1900-01-01 for a datetime column
The profile is selected before the update, so the user sees the previous login time

confirmedRules.name: Program access by super-user flag or role membership
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Super users can open every active, non-deleted program. Other users can open only the active, non-deleted programs where they hold a non-deleted membership in an active, non-deleted role.
confirmedRules.given: Programs 1, 2 and 3 are active. User 'jsmith' (IsSuperUser=0) is a member of an active role in program 2 only. User 'admin' has IsSuperUser=1.
confirmedRules.then: 'jsmith' gets program list [2] and 'admin' gets [1,2,3]. Both lists are ordered by ProgId.
confirmedRules.parameters: Original source database/FLT_Schema.sql:6773-6816. Conditions: Program.IsActive=1 AND IsDeleted=0. For non-super users, also FltUserInRole.IsDeleted=0, FltRole.IsActive=1, FltRole.IsDeleted=0, and FltRole.ProgId = Program.ProgId.
edgeCases: FltUserInRole.IsActive is not checked; only its IsDeleted flag is
A user with several roles in the same program gets that program more than once (no DISTINCT)
The user's DefaultProgId is not checked against the list of allowed programs
A non-super user with no qualifying role gets an empty program list but still logs in successfully

confirmedRules.name: Aircraft accumulated flight usage (Hobbs total)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: An aircraft's current usage is the sum of (Hobbs end minus Hobbs start) over all of its active, non-deleted flights. An aircraft with no flights shows 0.
confirmedRules.given: Aircraft 10 has active flights with Hobbs 100.0-102.5 and 102.5-104.0, plus one deleted flight of 3.0 hours
confirmedRules.then: CurrentUsage = 2.5 + 1.5 = 4.0 hours. The deleted flight is excluded. The value is shown next to TotalRequiredUsage.
confirmedRules.parameters: Original source database/FLT_Schema.sql:12905-12937. Result type DECIMAL(8,1), maximum 9,999,999.9. Flight filter: IsActive=1 AND IsDeleted=0. Default 0 through ISNULL.

rejectedRules.name: Input text format rules
rejectedRules.plainEnglish: User names must start with a letter and may contain letters, digits, space, period, dash, underscore without doubling separators; file types must be a period followed by alphanumerics; MIME types, document names and common text fields are restricted to safe character sets; each pattern can be overridden in configuration.
rejectedRules.parameters: UserName ^[A-Za-z]{1}([A-Za-z0-9 ._-](?:(?![ ]{2}|[.]{2}|[_]{2}|[-]{2})))*$; FileType ^\.([A-Za-z0-9])*$; MimeType ^([A-Za-z0-9 .\/_-])*$; Common ^([A-Za-z0-9 .#\/()_-])*$; DocumentName: no OS-invalid filename chars; config keys UserNameRegEx, FileTypeRegEx, MimeTypeString, CommonRegEx
edgeCases: Empty strings pass FileType? No - '.' required; but '.' alone passes
Empty string passes MimeType and Common patterns
Common pattern allows '#' and parentheses though its message does not mention them
rejectedRules.suspectedDefect: MIME override reads config key 'MimeTypeString' while the message reads 'MimeTypeRegExMessage'; inconsistent naming suggests the override key may be wrong.
rejectedRules.rejectionReason:
refuted: The patterns and config keys in the rule match the code. The rule's own worked example is wrong, though, so it fails as a spec.

What matches, in ObjectPropertyValidator.vb:
- ValidateUserNameString (lines 50-62): the default regex is exactly as quoted. It is overridden by AppSettings("UserNameRegEx").
- ValidateFileTypeString (lines 64-76): `^\.([A-Za-z0-9])*$`, overridden by "FileTypeRegEx".
- ValidateMimeTypeString (lines 78-90): `^([A-Za-z0-9 .\/_-])*$`, overridden by key "MimeTypeString".
- ValidateDocumentNameString (lines 92-99): rejects any character from Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars(). It has no config override, so "each pattern can be overridden" is not true for DocumentName.
- ValidateCommonString (lines 101-113): `^([A-Za-z0-9 .#\/()_-])*$`, overridden by "CommonRegEx".

What fails: the example says 'j..doe' is rejected. I ran the exact pattern through a regex engine and 'j..doe' is ACCEPTED. 'jo..e' and 'john..doe' are rejected, and '.pdf' passes the FileType pattern as stated.

Why: the double-separator check `(?!...)` only runs after characters matched by the repeating group, never after the first letter matched by `[A-Za-z]{1}`. So a doubled separator right after the first letter is let through.

Corrected rule: doubled separators are rejected except directly after the first character. A valid example is 'john..doe' rejected, '.pdf' accepted. DocumentName has no config override.

Other notes:
- The default user-name message (line 11) does not mention that spaces are allowed, but the regex accepts them.
- Line 82 reads the override from the key "MimeTypeString", while the message (line 28) uses "MimeTypeRegExMessage".
- No instruction-shaped text found.

rejectedRules.name: Engineer and mechanic comments carry a component, issue code, rating and dated entry
rejectedRules.plainEnglish: Each engineer or mechanic comment on a work order names a component and an issue code, has a numeric rating and comment text, and its comment date must be a valid date or the save fails.
rejectedRules.given: An engineer comment on work order #1001 for component 12, issue code 4, rating 3, date "2026-10-14"
rejectedRules.then: The comment is stored with the date converted by CDate; a date like "tomorrow" makes CDate throw and the whole work order save is rolled back
rejectedRules.parameters: CommentRating SmallInt; ComponentId, IssueCodeId Int; CommentDate DateTime via CDate. Mechanic comments use the same rule (WOMechanicCommentDB.vb:203-216). Parts store PartNbrFailed/Removed/Added as integers via CInt (WorkOrderPartDB.vb:205-215), so non-numeric part numbers also fail the save.
edgeCases: No range check on rating in this layer
Part numbers with letters or dashes cannot be stored because they are converted with CInt
rejectedRules.smeQuestion: What is the valid rating scale for comments, and are part numbers really always whole numbers?
rejectedRules.rejectionReason: refuted: Lines 203-213 of WOEngineerCommentDB.vb only bind parameters for the updateWOEngineerComment stored procedure: ComponentId Int, CommentDate DateTime via CDate, CommentRating SmallInt, IssueCodeId Int, and Comments. That matches the rule's data shape. It does not implement the validation the rule claims ("a date like 'tomorrow' makes CDate throw and the whole work order save is rolled back"). The value passed to CDate at line 208 comes from the CommentDate property getter in WOEngineerComment.vb:84-99. That getter always returns Format(_commentDate, "MM-dd-yyyy") from a Date field, so CDate always gets a well-formed date string and cannot throw on user input. Invalid input is caught earlier. The setter checks IsDate(value) and quietly sets _commentDate = Nothing when the check fails (lines 90-94). The business object's validation then records a broken rule, "CommentDate is required" with code 03-01-003, at WOEngineerComment.vb:280-284. The same validation also limits the rating to 1-10 (03-01-004, lines 285-286), which the rule does not mention. So the real date and rating validation is in the business object, not at the cited data-access lines, and the cited CDate is not a guard. The data-access code does sit inside the shared work order transaction (WorkOrderDB.vb:540-554), but the specific failure the rule describes cannot happen through this path. No instruction-shaped text was found in the cited region.

rejectedRules.name: Fleet board sorting and auto-refresh
rejectedRules.plainEnglish: The fleet board is sorted by Location by default, can be re-sorted by Location, MSN (FRC #) or Last Update Date, and reloads every 5 seconds.
rejectedRules.given: A user opens the main fleet board
rejectedRules.when: The page loads with no sort chosen
rejectedRules.then: Rows are ordered by Location, and the page refreshes itself every 5 seconds while keeping the chosen sort

edgeCases: Status is colour-coded: UP is green with white text and DOWN is red with black text. OFF TEST has no highlight
The sort value comes from a hidden field the client can change. The stored procedure must whitelist it
rejectedRules.rejectionReason:
refuted: Most of the rule holds, but its Then clause makes a claim the code doesn't support, so I can't confirm it as written.

What the code does:
- Default sort is Location: `_SortingColumn = "Location"` is set at FltFleet/Default.aspx.vb:10. On a first load (not a postback), Page_Load saves it to SortByHiddenField (Default.aspx.vb:21-25).
- Users can re-sort by Location, MSN or Date: the column SortExpressions are at FltFleet/Default.aspx:44, 47 and 55. FleetGridView_Sorting (Default.aspx.vb:77-85) stores the chosen sort in the hidden field and binds the grid again.
- The sort key goes to the database: AircraftStatusManager.GetList passes it (Default.aspx.vb:33), and the stored procedure branches on @SortBy = 'Location' / 'MSN' / 'Date' (database/FLT_Schema.sql:13353, 13379-13391).
- The page refreshes every 5 seconds: `<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="5">` at FltFleet/Default.aspx:10.
- The OFF TEST page has no refresh: OffTestFleet.aspx contains no refresh meta tag.

What the code does not do:
- The rule says the refresh keeps the chosen sort. It doesn't. A meta refresh reloads the page with a plain GET, not a form postback. So on each refresh `IsPostBack` is False and the else branch at Default.aspx.vb:23-24 writes the default "Location" back into SortByHiddenField. The hidden field only carries the sort across postbacks such as paging or clicking a column header.
- Result: within about 5 seconds of choosing MSN or Date, the board goes back to sorting by Location. The rule states the opposite, so the specification has to be corrected before this can be confirmed.

I found no instruction-shaped text at the cited lines.

rejectedRules.smeQuestion: Was Flight_Unique meant to include DuplicateCount, so historical duplicates are kept but new ones are blocked? Has this script ever been run successfully in production?
rejectedRules.rejectionReason: refuted: The cited script (/Users/jccex/Development/flight-log-workshop/DuplicateFlightKeyImplementation.sql) does contain the logic, but as written it cannot produce the result the rule claims. What matches: lines 9-10 add DuplicateCount INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (0). Lines 24-37 select groups with HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 on (AircraftId, LocationId, FlightDateSort, WorkShiftIndicatorId). Lines 44-65 reset @Count to 0 and set DuplicateCount = 0,1,2... in FlightId order using WHERE CURRENT OF. Four defects mean the stated outcome never happens. (1) Line 72 reads 'FETCH NEXT FROM curFlights', but the cursor declared on line 24 is named curFlights1. That cursor name does not exist, so at most the first duplicate group gets numbered before a runtime error. The outer loop also never advances correctly. (2) Line 79 'EXECUTE zFix_Set_Flight_DuplicateCount()' is invalid T-SQL because of the parentheses, so the procedure is never run by this script. (3) Line 82 'ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT [Flight_Unique] ...' leaves out the table name and is a syntax error, so the constraint is never added. (4) Even with these fixed, the UNIQUE key is only the four original columns and leaves out DuplicateCount. The duplicate rows the procedure numbers would still break that key, so adding the constraint would fail. The design intent is clearly to include DuplicateCount in the key. The rule's 'Then a UNIQUE constraint Flight_Unique is added on (AircraftId, LocationId, FlightDateSort, WorkShiftIndicatorId)' is therefore false, and numbering every duplicate group is not achieved. The rule describes what the script was meant to do, not what it does. Report it as a broken or never-completed migration, not as an enforced lifecycle rule. No instruction-shaped text or credentials in the cited lines.
